semanticNote: A case in the sense of a documented example or precedent — used in medicine (病例 is more medical-specific), law (legal precedent), business analysis, education. Different from 案件 (a legal/criminal case being investigated) — 案例 is the studied example, 案件 is the active case. 案例研究 = case study.

examples.chinese: 這是一個成功的商業案例。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge chénggōng de shāngyè ànlì.
examples.english: This is a successful business case.

examples.chinese: 醫生分享了一個有趣的案例。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng fēnxiǎngle yí ge yǒuqù de ànlì.
examples.english: The doctor shared an interesting case.

semanticNote: Both verb and noun. To convey something indirectly — through tone, gesture, or oblique words rather than saying it outright. Often used when someone hints at desire, opinion, or expectation without committing. 心理暗示 = psychological suggestion (the placebo-adjacent meaning). Compare to 提示 (to remind / cue, more neutral) and 明說 (to say outright).

examples.chinese: 她的眼神暗示我該離開了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yǎnshén ànshì wǒ gāi líkāile.
examples.english: Her look hinted that I should leave.

examples.chinese: 他暗示他想要加薪。
examples.pinyin: Tā ànshì tā xiǎng yào jiāxīn.
examples.english: He hinted that he wanted a raise.

semanticNote: More formal and emphatic than 貴 — suggests significantly, even prohibitively expensive. Used in writing and serious speech: 昂貴的代價 (a costly price), 昂貴的禮物 (an expensive gift). In casual conversation Taiwanese speakers just say 貴. Reach for 昂貴 when the cost is notable enough to warrant comment.

examples.chinese: 這款手錶非常昂貴。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn shǒubiǎo fēicháng ángguì.
examples.english: This watch is extremely expensive.

examples.chinese: 我們付出了昂貴的代價。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen fùchūle ángguì de dàijià.
examples.english: We paid a costly price.

semanticNote: Visual/textural word — surfaces with raised and recessed patterns. The two characters literally look like what they mean: 凹 (concave/dip) and 凸 (convex/bump). Used for road surfaces, fabric textures, terrain, even faces (凹凸有致 = well-defined features). 凹凸不平 = uneven (very common collocation). One of the rare Chinese words where you can teach the meaning by just pointing at the characters.

examples.chinese: 這條路面凹凸不平。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lùmiàn āotū bùpíng.
examples.english: The surface of this road is bumpy and uneven.

examples.chinese: 她有著凹凸有致的身材。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒuzhe āotū yǒuzhì de shēncái.
examples.english: She has a well-defined figure.

english: to endure; to simmer / boil down
semanticNote: Two cooking-derived senses that bleed into each other: (1) literally simmer or boil down — 熬湯 (simmer soup), 熬粥 (cook congee), long slow heat; (2) figuratively endure something difficult through to the other side — 熬夜 (stay up late / pull an all-nighter), 熬過去 (get through it), 熬出頭 (finally emerge from hardship). The metaphor is beautiful: enduring hardship is like slow-cooking yourself.

examples.chinese: 我昨天熬夜寫報告。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān áoyè xiě bàogào.
examples.english: I stayed up all night yesterday writing a report.

examples.chinese: 媽媽正在廚房熬雞湯。
examples.pinyin: Māma zhèngzài chúfáng áo jītāng.
examples.english: Mom is in the kitchen simmering chicken soup.

semanticNote: A deep mystery — the kind worth investigating, contemplating, or revealing. Used for the mysteries of nature (大自然的奧秘), the universe (宇宙的奧秘), the human mind, ancient cultures. Has a slight reverent or awe-struck flavor that 秘密 (a regular secret) doesn't carry. 揭開奧秘 = unveil the mystery. Literary register.

examples.chinese: 科學家在探索宇宙的奧秘。
examples.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā zài tànsuǒ yǔzhòu de àomì.
examples.english: Scientists are exploring the mysteries of the universe.

examples.chinese: 這部紀錄片揭開了海洋的奧秘。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù jìlùpiàn jiēkāile hǎiyáng de àomì.
examples.english: This documentary unveils the mysteries of the ocean.

english: to be eager to; can't wait to
semanticNote: Spoken-Mandarin staple expressing intense eagerness — 'I'd give anything to' or 'I can't wait to.' Often expresses an unfulfilled wish: 我巴不得馬上下班 = I'd love nothing more than to clock out right now. Slightly exaggerated, almost confessional in tone. Compare to 希望 (neutral 'hope') and 渴望 (formal 'long for'). 巴不得 has the most desperate/eager flavor.

examples.chinese: 我巴不得現在就放假。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bābùdé xiànzài jiù fàngjià.
examples.english: I can't wait for the holidays to start right now.

examples.chinese: 他巴不得搬出去住。
examples.pinyin: Tā bābùdé bān chūqù zhù.
examples.english: He's dying to move out.

english: to suck up to; curry favor with
semanticNote: Negative-flavored: to fawn over someone in power for personal gain. Implies shamelessness or transparency in the flattery — others can see through it. Targets are usually bosses, wealthy people, officials. Compare to 討好 (please / try to get on someone's good side, milder, less judgmental) and 拍馬屁 (a vivid colloquial idiom: literally 'pat the horse's butt' — same act, more humorous tone).

examples.chinese: 他總是巴結老闆。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì bājié lǎobǎn.
examples.english: He's always sucking up to the boss.

examples.chinese: 我不喜歡他那種巴結人的樣子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xǐhuān tā nà zhǒng bājié rén de yàngzi.
examples.english: I don't like the way he sucks up to people.

english: to cling to; to dig up; to peel; to pickpocket
semanticNote: Range of physical actions involving hands grabbing, scraping, or peeling: 扒著欄杆 (clinging to a railing), 扒開葉子 (push leaves apart), 扒皮 (peel skin off). Heteronym alert: read pá it means to crawl or rake (扒手 = pickpocket — but pronounced pá-shǒu). The bā reading dominates HSK 6 contexts. Often appears in compounds — rarely standalone in modern speech.

examples.chinese: 孩子扒著窗戶往外看。
examples.pinyin: Háizi bāzhe chuānghu wǎngwài kàn.
examples.english: The child clung to the window looking out.

examples.chinese: 他扒開草叢找鑰匙。
examples.pinyin: Tā bā kāi cǎocóng zhǎo yàoshi.
examples.english: He pushed the grass aside looking for the keys.

semanticNote: A scar on skin, or any mark left by a wound. Often appears as 疤痕 (scar mark — fuller form). 留疤 = leave a scar. Used both literally (傷疤 = wound scar) and figuratively for emotional/psychological scars (心靈的傷疤). Concrete, visceral word — not literary.

examples.chinese: 他的臉上有一道疤。
examples.pinyin: Tā de liǎn shàng yǒu yí dào bā.
examples.english: He has a scar on his face.

examples.chinese: 這個傷口可能會留疤。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge shāngkǒu kěnéng huì liú bā.
examples.english: This wound might leave a scar.

english: to spoil things through forced haste (idiom)
semanticNote: Famous chengyu from a Mencius story: a farmer pulls his rice seedlings up to make them 'grow taller' and ends up killing them. Used to criticize impatient parenting, rushed education, premature scaling — anything where forcing speed sabotages the natural process. Particularly common in discussions of child-rearing and learning. The story is well-known enough that even saying just 拔苗 is often understood.

examples.chinese: 教育孩子不能拔苗助長。
examples.pinyin: Jiàoyù háizi bùnéng bámiáozhùzhǎng.
examples.english: You can't rush a child's education by force.

examples.chinese: 他這樣訓練只會拔苗助長。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhèyàng xùnliàn zhǐ huì bámiáozhùzhǎng.
examples.english: Training like this will only backfire.

english: to guard a pass; to check / vet
semanticNote: Originally military — to guard a mountain pass. Modern usage: to act as a quality gatekeeper, vet things before they pass through. 嚴格把關 = vet rigorously. Used in editorial work, manufacturing QC, hiring, content moderation. Implies responsibility and judgment, not just inspection. 為品質把關 = guarantee the quality.

examples.chinese: 編輯負責為文章把關。
examples.pinyin: Biānjí fùzé wèi wénzhāng bǎguān.
examples.english: The editor is responsible for vetting the articles.

examples.chinese: 我們對產品品質嚴格把關。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen duì chǎnpǐn pǐnzhì yángé bǎguān.
examples.english: We rigorously check our product quality.

semanticNote: The handle of a thing — a door, a cup, a tool, a drawer. Concrete physical object. Note the alternate reading bàshou which means 'crony / sworn brother' in some compounds (一把手 = top dog, top boss — totally different sense). For HSK 6 the bǎshǒu reading meaning 'handle' is the target.

examples.chinese: 門的把手壞了。
examples.pinyin: Mén de bǎshǒu huàile.
examples.english: The door handle is broken.

examples.chinese: 請抓住扶梯的把手。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zhuāzhù fútī de bǎshǒu.
examples.english: Please hold onto the escalator's handrail.

semanticNote: Labor strike — workers refusing to work to demand better conditions. Both noun and verb. Common in news contexts: 大罷工 (general strike), 發動罷工 (call a strike), 罷工抗議 (strike in protest). The 罷 character is also in 罷課 (student strike) and 罷免 (recall an official from office). Politically loaded word in mainland press; more neutral in Taiwan.

examples.chinese: 工人決定罷工。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrén juédìng bàgōng.
examples.english: The workers decided to go on strike.

examples.chinese: 這次罷工持續了一個星期。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì bàgōng chíxùle yí ge xīngqī.
examples.english: This strike lasted a week.

semanticNote: Describes someone who imposes their will without regard for others — bullying, autocratic. Originally a political term (rule by force) contrasted with 王道 (rule by virtue). Modern usage: an overbearing boss, a tyrannical parent, a pushy partner. Romance-novel trope: 霸道總裁 (the domineering CEO love interest) is a whole genre. Negative when describing real people, sometimes admiring/aspirational in fiction.

examples.chinese: 他在家裡很霸道。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jiā lǐ hěn bàdào.
examples.english: He's very domineering at home.

examples.chinese: 這種做法太霸道了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng zuòfǎ tài bàdào le.
examples.english: This way of doing things is too overbearing.

english: to break apart with hands; (slang) to make up / fabricate
semanticNote: Physical: to break something with two hands, like snapping a piece of bread or a wafer in two — 掰開 (break open). The character itself is a pictograph: two hands (手) splitting something in the middle. Slang: to fabricate / make up (a story, an excuse) — 瞎掰 (talking nonsense). Also 掰了 in casual relationship-speak = 'we broke up.' Punchy, colloquial word.

examples.chinese: 她把巧克力掰成兩半。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ qiǎokèlì bāichéng liǎng bàn.
examples.english: She broke the chocolate into two halves.

examples.chinese: 別瞎掰了，我不信。
examples.pinyin: Bié xiā bāi le, wǒ bú xìn.
examples.english: Stop making stuff up, I don't believe you.

english: to break free from; shake off
semanticNote: To free oneself from something unwanted — debt, addiction, bad habits, an annoying person, a difficult situation, the past. Strong sense of effortful liberation, not just leaving. 擺脫困境 (break free from a predicament), 擺脫貧困 (escape poverty), 擺脫他 (shake him off). Differs from 離開 (just 'leave'); 擺脫 implies something was holding on.

examples.chinese: 他終於擺脫了壞習慣。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú bǎituōle huài xíguàn.
examples.english: He finally broke free from his bad habit.

examples.chinese: 我想擺脫這些煩惱。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bǎituō zhèxiē fánnǎo.
examples.english: I want to shake off these worries.

semanticNote: To corrupt or ruin something abstract — morals, social customs, reputation, atmosphere. 敗壞風氣 (corrupt social mores), 敗壞名聲 (ruin a reputation). Has strong moral judgment built in — you don't 敗壞 a building or a meal, you 敗壞 things people are supposed to keep good. Formal/serious register. Literary echo: pairs with concepts of decay, decline, moral rot.

examples.chinese: 他的行為敗壞了公司的名聲。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xíngwéi bàihuàile gōngsī de míngshēng.
examples.english: His behavior ruined the company's reputation.

examples.chinese: 這種風氣正在敗壞社會。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng fēngqì zhèngzài bàihuài shèhuì.
examples.english: This trend is corrupting society.

english: to call on; pay a visit (formal)
semanticNote: A respectful visit — to a senior, an elder, a client, a teacher. The 拜 component carries deference (it appears in 拜年 'pay New Year respects' and 拜託 'please / I beg you'). Compare to 看 (just 'see/visit', casual), 探望 (visit someone sick or older, caring), 訪問 (formal/official visit, often interview). 拜訪 lands in 'respectful, intentional visit with social weight.'

examples.chinese: 明天我要拜訪一位客戶。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān wǒ yào bàifǎng yí wèi kèhù.
examples.english: Tomorrow I'm going to call on a client.

examples.chinese: 他特地去拜訪老師。
examples.pinyin: Tā tèdì qù bàifǎng lǎoshī.
examples.english: He made a special trip to visit his teacher.

english: to pay a New Year visit; wish someone Happy New Year
semanticNote: The Chinese New Year ritual of visiting family, friends, neighbors during the first days of the lunar new year to exchange greetings and well-wishes. Children 拜年 to elders, often receiving 紅包 (red envelopes) in return. Now also done by phone, video call, message. Cultural cornerstone — knowing this word means knowing the ritual. 給您拜年 = (politely) wishing you a Happy New Year.

examples.chinese: 大年初一我們去爺爺家拜年。
examples.pinyin: Dà nián chū yī wǒmen qù yéye jiā bàinián.
examples.english: On New Year's Day we go to Grandpa's house to pay our respects.

examples.chinese: 我打電話給朋友拜年。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dǎ diànhuà gěi péngyǒu bàinián.
examples.english: I called my friend to wish them Happy New Year.

english: please; I beg you; (politely) ask a favor
semanticNote: Chameleon word with two main lives: (1) verb — 'to entrust someone with a favor': 我拜託你幫我看一下 (please help me look at this for a sec); (2) standalone interjection — 'Come on!' / 'Please!' / 'Seriously?' depending on tone. The interjection use is huge in Taiwanese spoken Mandarin: 拜託! 我又不是三歲小孩 (Come on, I'm not three years old). Carries either real politeness or playful exasperation depending on context.

examples.chinese: 拜託你別再遲到了。
examples.pinyin: Bàituō nǐ bié zài chídàole.
examples.english: Please stop being late.

examples.chinese: 拜託，這也太誇張了吧！
examples.pinyin: Bàituō, zhè yě tài kuāzhāng le ba!
examples.english: Come on, that's way too over the top!

semanticNote: Official act of issuing laws, regulations, decrees, awards. Subject is always an authority — government, court, ministry, sometimes school administration. 頒佈法律 (promulgate a law), 頒佈命令 (issue an order). Compare to 發佈 (release / announce, more general) and 公布 (publicize, broader). 頒佈 has the most formal/official ring.

examples.chinese: 政府頒佈了新的環保法規。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ bānbùle xīn de huánbǎo fǎguī.
examples.english: The government issued new environmental regulations.

examples.chinese: 這項法律明年才會頒佈。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng fǎlǜ míngnián cái huì bānbù.
examples.english: This law won't be promulgated until next year.

semanticNote: To issue or award something formal — a prize, certificate, license, medal, honor. Subject is the awarding body. 頒發獎牌 (award a medal), 頒發證書 (issue a certificate). Sister-word to 頒佈 — 頒發 awards things to recipients, 頒佈 promulgates rules to the public. Ceremonial, honorific flavor.

examples.chinese: 校長親自頒發獎學金。
examples.pinyin: Xiàozhǎng qīnzì bānfā jiǎngxuéjīn.
examples.english: The principal personally presented the scholarship.

examples.chinese: 公司向優秀員工頒發獎品。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī xiàng yōuxiù yuángōng bānfā jiǎngpǐn.
examples.english: The company gives prizes to outstanding employees.

semanticNote: A spot or marking — freckles (雀斑), age spots (老人斑), animal markings (斑馬 = zebra, literally 'striped horse'), stains. Often appears in compounds rather than alone: 斑點 (spots), 黑斑 (dark spot/mole). Used metaphorically too — 可見一斑 (literally 'one spot is visible' = a glimpse reveals the whole, like seeing a leopard through a tube).

examples.chinese: 她臉上有很多雀斑。
examples.pinyin: Tā liǎn shàng yǒu hěn duō quèbān.
examples.english: She has a lot of freckles on her face.

examples.chinese: 這隻貓身上有黑斑。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī māo shēn shàng yǒu hēi bān.
examples.english: This cat has black spots on its body.

semanticNote: Version of something — a book edition, software release, or even a story (different people's versions of events). Tech context dominates: 軟體版本 (software version), 最新版本 (latest version), 升級版本 (upgrade the version). Also 中文版本 (Chinese version), 電子版本 (electronic edition). Replaces older 版 in most modern contexts.

examples.chinese: 請更新到最新版本。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gēngxīn dào zuì xīn bǎnběn.
examples.english: Please update to the latest version.

examples.chinese: 這本書有兩個版本。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yǒu liǎng ge bǎnběn.
examples.english: This book has two editions.

semanticNote: To abandon a project or pursuit halfway through — usually a criticism. Often used by parents, teachers, coaches: 不要半途而廢 (don't give up halfway). Implies wasted effort and weak resolve. Common opposite: 堅持到底 (persist to the end). Literary register but used in everyday admonishment.

examples.chinese: 做事不能半途而廢。
examples.pinyin: Zuòshì bùnéng bàntú'érfèi.
examples.english: You can't give up halfway when doing things.

examples.chinese: 他學中文學到一半就半途而廢了。
examples.pinyin: Tā xué Zhōngwén xué dào yíbàn jiù bàntú'érfèile.
examples.english: He gave up halfway through learning Chinese.

english: to play the role of; act as
semanticNote: Theatrical: to play a character on stage or screen — 扮演主角 (play the lead). Figurative: to take on a role in life or a situation — 扮演重要的角色 (play an important role) is one of the most common collocations in formal/business Chinese. Different from 演 (more general 'perform/act') — 扮演 specifically emphasizes embodying a character.

components.meaning: to dress as; play a role

examples.chinese: 她在電影裡扮演女主角。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài diànyǐng lǐ bànyǎn nǚ zhǔjiǎo.
examples.english: She plays the female lead in the movie.

examples.chinese: 教育在社會中扮演重要的角色。
examples.pinyin: Jiàoyù zài shèhuì zhōng bànyǎn zhòngyào de juésè.
examples.english: Education plays an important role in society.

semanticNote: Life partner — romantic companion, often used for spouses or long-term partners. Slightly more thoughtful and warm than 配偶 (legal spouse, paperwork-flavored). 終身伴侶 = lifelong partner. Increasingly inclusive in modern usage — covers same-sex partners and unmarried partners, where 配偶 implies legal marriage. Literary echo: 良伴 (a good companion).

examples.chinese: 她終於找到了人生的伴侶。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú zhǎodàole rénshēng de bànlǚ.
examples.english: She finally found her life partner.

examples.chinese: 他們是一對恩愛的伴侶。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shì yí duì ēn'ài de bànlǚ.
examples.english: They're a loving couple.

english: to accompany; go along with; be accompanied by
semanticNote: To go alongside something — usually used for abstract things that come together: success accompanied by stress, growth accompanied by pain, technology accompanied by new problems. 伴隨而來 = come along with. More formal than 跟著 (follow) and more abstract than 陪 (keep someone company). News and analytical writing love this word: 伴隨經濟發展... (accompanying economic development...).

examples.chinese: 成功往往伴隨著壓力。
examples.pinyin: Chénggōng wǎngwǎng bànsuízhe yālì.
examples.english: Success is often accompanied by stress.

examples.chinese: 伴隨著科技的發展，生活更便利了。
examples.pinyin: Bànsuízhe kējì de fāzhǎn, shēnghuó gèng biànlìle.
examples.english: With the development of technology, life has become more convenient.

semanticNote: Literal kidnapping — usually for ransom. Also used metaphorically and politically: 道德綁架 (moral kidnapping — manipulating someone via moral pressure / guilt-tripping) is a very common modern term in social commentary. 情感綁架 = emotional blackmail. The metaphorical extension is now arguably more common in everyday discourse than the literal sense.

examples.chinese: 歹徒綁架了那個富商。
examples.pinyin: Dǎitú bǎngjiàle nà ge fùshāng.
examples.english: The criminals kidnapped that wealthy businessman.

examples.chinese: 你這樣是道德綁架。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhèyàng shì dàodé bǎngjià.
examples.english: What you're doing is moral blackmail.

semanticNote: A model to be emulated — a positive example. Used for teachers, parents, leaders, exemplary figures. 樹立榜樣 (set an example), 成為榜樣 (become a role model), 學習榜樣 (one to learn from). Always positive (unlike 例子 which is a neutral example, or 反面教材 which is a 'negative example' / cautionary tale). Common in education and parenting talk.

examples.chinese: 父母是孩子最好的榜樣。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ shì háizi zuìhǎo de bǎngyàng.
examples.english: Parents are the best role models for children.

examples.chinese: 他是我們學習的榜樣。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen xuéxí de bǎngyàng.
examples.english: He's a role model we should learn from.

semanticNote: The imperial weight unit (pound, ~454g). Also the scale for weighing — 磅秤 (scale). 一磅 = one pound. Mostly encountered in Taiwan in fitness/diet contexts (where pounds compete with kilograms for daily use), gym weights, and translated content. Mainland uses 斤 (~500g) as the everyday unit.

examples.chinese: 我這個月瘦了三磅。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhè ge yuè shòule sān bàng.
examples.english: I lost three pounds this month.

examples.chinese: 請幫我磅一下這個包裹。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ bàng yíxià zhè ge bāoguǒ.
examples.english: Please weigh this package for me.

english: to shield (a wrongdoer); cover up for
semanticNote: Specifically to protect someone who has done wrong — covering up their crime, mistake, or wrongdoing. Always negative. Used in legal/political contexts: 包庇罪犯 (shield a criminal), 互相包庇 (cover for each other). Compare to 保護 (just protect, neutral) and 庇護 (give sanctuary, can be neutral).

examples.chinese: 他被指控包庇下屬。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi zhǐkòng bāobì xiàshǔ.
examples.english: He was accused of covering up for his subordinates.

semanticNote: Literal: a bundle wrapped in cloth (the old way travelers carried things). Figurative (now dominant): a psychological burden or baggage — 思想包袱 (mental burden), 歷史包袱 (historical baggage), 卸下包袱 (unload the burden). Also has a comedy meaning — 抖包袱 = deliver the punchline (like opening a bundle to reveal what's inside).

examples.chinese: 別讓過去成為你的包袱。
examples.pinyin: Bié ràng guòqù chéngwéi nǐ de bāofu.
examples.english: Don't let the past become your baggage.

semanticNote: To completely surround something or someone — military (encircle the enemy), crowd (the celebrity was mobbed), or figuratively (被問題包圍 = surrounded by problems). Implies no escape route. Stronger than 圍 alone, which can just mean 'gather around.'

examples.chinese: 警察包圍了那棟大樓。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá bāowéile nà dòng dàlóu.
examples.english: The police surrounded the building.

semanticNote: Both verb and noun. Literal: package a product (產品包裝). Figurative: 'package' a person, brand, or idea — to dress it up for presentation (包裝自己 = market yourself, repackage your image). Common in marketing and entertainment — 包裝歌手 = grooming a singer for stardom. Carries a slight 'putting on a show' undertone in figurative use.

examples.chinese: 這個禮物的包裝很漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge lǐwù de bāozhuāng hěn piàoliàng.
examples.english: This gift's packaging is beautiful.

examples.chinese: 公司花錢包裝這位新人。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī huā qián bāozhuāng zhè wèi xīnrén.
examples.english: The company spent money grooming this newcomer's image.

semanticNote: Technical-origin word now common in business and casual contexts. Literal: solution saturation. Figurative: a market is saturated (市場飽和), one's stomach is full (very colloquial 我吃飽和了 — though usually just 飽), schedule is fully booked. 達到飽和 = reach saturation. Tipping-point word.

examples.chinese: 這個市場已經飽和了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge shìchǎng yǐjīng bǎohé le.
examples.english: This market is already saturated.

semanticNote: Literally 'fully experienced the [transformation of] sea into mulberry fields' — a classical image of vast historical change. Used to describe people (especially old people) who have lived through hard times, or places/buildings that have witnessed history. Reverent, slightly melancholic flavor. Common in essays and tributes: 飽經滄桑的老人 (an old man who's seen it all).

examples.chinese: 這位飽經滄桑的老人有許多故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi bǎojīngcāngsāng de lǎorén yǒu xǔduō gùshì.
examples.english: This old man, who has weathered so much, has many stories.

english: to take charge of; safekeep; (colloquially) guarantee
semanticNote: Two senses: (1) to safeguard / take custody of valuables, documents, items entrusted to you — 保管錢包 (look after a wallet); (2) colloquial 'guarantee' / 'I assure you' — 我保管沒問題 (I guarantee no problem). The guarantee sense is very Northern/Mainland-flavored, less common in Taiwan. Don't confuse with 保證 (formal guarantee).

examples.chinese: 請幫我保管這個包包。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ bǎoguǎn zhè ge bāobāo.
examples.english: Please look after this bag for me.

semanticNote: Verb-object compound: 保 (keep) + 密 (secret). To maintain confidentiality about something. 嚴格保密 (strictly confidential), 替我保密 (keep my secret). Used in serious contexts (work secrets, government, personal confidences) — not for casual surprises (which would be 別說出去). Often appears as 保密協議 (NDA, non-disclosure agreement).

examples.chinese: 請幫我保密。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ bǎomì.
examples.english: Please keep this confidential for me.

semanticNote: Hired caregiver, primarily for children but also for the elderly or sick. 月嫂 = postpartum care nanny (specialized). In Taiwan, 保母 (alternate writing) is more common. Used metaphorically too: 我不是你的保姆 (I'm not your babysitter — common parental retort to a slacking spouse or kid).

examples.chinese: 她請了一個保姆來照顧寶寶。
examples.pinyin: Tā qǐngle yí ge bǎomǔ lái zhàogù bǎobao.
examples.english: She hired a nanny to take care of the baby.

semanticNote: Two main uses: (1) adjective — conservative, in politics (保守派 = conservatives), in personal style (保守的衣服 = conservative clothing), or in estimates (保守估計 = conservative estimate); (2) verb — to keep/guard (保守秘密 = keep a secret). The political sense vs. the 'keep secret' sense are quite different — context disambiguates.

examples.chinese: 他的觀念比較保守。
examples.pinyin: Tā de guānniàn bǐjiào bǎoshǒu.
examples.english: His views are relatively conservative.

examples.chinese: 請保守這個秘密。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎoshǒu zhè ge mìmì.
examples.english: Please keep this secret.

semanticNote: To actively defend something important — country, freedom, honor, family, peace. Carries a heroic / dutiful flavor. 保衛祖國 (defend the motherland), 保衛和平 (safeguard peace). More martial/active than 保護 (protect, broader and gentler). Often appears in patriotic and military contexts.

examples.chinese: 軍人的責任是保衛國家。
examples.pinyin: Jūnrén de zérèn shì bǎowèi guójiā.
examples.english: A soldier's duty is to defend the country.

english: to maintain (health, car); take good care of
semanticNote: Maintenance-flavored care — preserving the condition of something over time. Three big domains: (1) skin/body — 皮膚保養 (skincare); (2) vehicles — 汽車保養 (car maintenance / servicing); (3) general health (注意保養 = take care of yourself, said to elders). Different from 保護 (protect from harm) — 保養 is ongoing upkeep.

examples.chinese: 她很注重皮膚保養。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn zhùzhòng pífū bǎoyǎng.
examples.english: She really focuses on skincare.

examples.chinese: 汽車該去保養了。
examples.pinyin: Qìchē gāi qù bǎoyǎng le.
examples.english: The car is due for servicing.

semanticNote: Both verb and noun. As a verb: to ensure that something is protected or available — 保障人民的權利 (safeguard the people's rights). As a noun: a guarantee, a safeguard — 社會保障 (social security). Very common in legal, political, and policy language. Stronger than 保證 (to promise/guarantee) — 保障 implies institutional backing or structural protection, not just a personal pledge. 保障 = systemic guarantee; 保證 = personal assurance.

examples.chinese: 政府有責任保障公民的基本權利。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ yǒu zérèn bǎozhàng gōngmín de jīběn quánlì.
examples.english: The government has a responsibility to safeguard citizens' basic rights.

examples.chinese: 完善的法律制度是社會穩定的保障。
examples.pinyin: Wánshàn de fǎlǜ zhìdù shì shèhuì wěndìng de bǎozhàng.
examples.english: A sound legal system is a guarantee of social stability.

semanticNote: A parting word — 'take care of yourself' — said to someone leaving on a journey, going through hardship, or just at the end of a heartfelt farewell. Warmer and more weighty than 再見. 多保重 = take extra care. Often in letters and goodbye scenes. Sincere word — not used casually.

examples.chinese: 路上保重。
examples.pinyin: Lùshàng bǎozhòng.
examples.english: Take care on your journey.

semanticNote: Specifically revenge for a serious wrong — usually the killing of a loved one in classical/dramatic contexts. Modern usage extends to lesser grievances but retains gravity. 為父報仇 (avenge one's father). Compare to 報復 (retaliate, broader and more modern), 復仇 (very literary/dramatic). 報仇 is the spoken middle ground.

examples.chinese: 他發誓要為哥哥報仇。
examples.pinyin: Tā fāshì yào wèi gēge bàochóu.
examples.english: He swore to avenge his brother.

semanticNote: Money or benefits paid for work or service rendered. More formal/general than 工資 (wages) or 薪水 (salary). Used when discussing the principle of compensation: 應得的報酬 (deserved compensation), 不計報酬 (without expecting reward). Common in business writing and discussions of fairness.

examples.chinese: 他付出努力,得到應有的報酬。
examples.pinyin: Tā fùchū nǔlì, dédào yīngyǒu de bàochou.
examples.english: He put in the effort and got the compensation he deserved.

semanticNote: To repay specifically a kindness — usually directed at parents, mentors, benefactors. Implies gratitude and obligation. 報答父母 (repay one's parents — a deeply Chinese cultural concept), 報答恩情 (repay the kindness). Different from 報復 (retaliate/get back at, negative) — 報答 is the positive flip side.

examples.chinese: 我永遠都會報答父母的養育之恩。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒngyuǎn dōu huì bàodá fùmǔ de yǎngyù zhī ēn.
examples.english: I will always repay my parents' kindness in raising me.

semanticNote: Modern, broad word for retaliation — petty (報復前任 = revenge against an ex), legal (報復性消費 = revenge spending), political, military. Always negative, implies tit-for-tat. Compare to 報仇 (more grave, classical). 報復心強 = vindictive. The everyday word for getting back at someone.

examples.chinese: 他想要報復那個陷害他的人。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng yào bàofù nà ge xiànhài tā de rén.
examples.english: He wants to get revenge on the person who framed him.

english: to call the police; report to the authorities
semanticNote: Specifically to call/notify the police about an incident. 我要報警! (I'm going to call the cops!) is the standard way to escalate a dispute. Also extends to fire/emergency reporting. 報警電話 = emergency hotline (110 in Taiwan and mainland).

examples.chinese: 再不離開我就報警了。
examples.pinyin: Zài bù líkāi wǒ jiù bàojǐng le.
examples.english: If you don't leave I'm calling the police.

english: to submit (expenses) for reimbursement; (slang) to be done for
semanticNote: Two senses: (1) the office word — submit receipts to be reimbursed (出差費可以報銷 = travel expenses are reimbursable); (2) slang/dark humor — 'done for / written off' as in destroyed or killed (這台電腦報銷了 = this computer is toast). Office workers will use both senses in the same week.

examples.chinese: 這頓飯可以報銷嗎？
examples.pinyin: Zhè dùn fàn kěyǐ bàoxiāo ma?
examples.english: Can this meal be reimbursed?

examples.chinese: 我的手機摔了一下就報銷了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī shuāile yíxià jiù bàoxiāo le.
examples.english: My phone took one fall and now it's toast.

semanticNote: Lofty personal ambition — a vision for what you want to accomplish in life. Positive flavor (unlike 野心 'ambition' which can be selfish/ruthless). 有抱負的年輕人 (an ambitious young person). Often paired with 理想 (ideals). Used in motivational and career contexts.

examples.chinese: 他是個有抱負的年輕人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge yǒu bàofù de niánqīngrén.
examples.english: He's an ambitious young man.

semanticNote: Physical violence — the abstract concept. 家庭暴力 (domestic violence), 暴力行為 (violent behavior). Also extends figuratively: 語言暴力 (verbal/online abuse), 冷暴力 (silent treatment as a form of relational abuse). Modern Mandarin has stretched 暴力 to cover many kinds of harm.

examples.chinese: 我們反對任何形式的暴力。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen fǎnduì rènhé xíngshì de bàolì.
examples.english: We oppose violence of any form.

semanticNote: To bring something previously hidden into view — usually negative things. Secrets, weaknesses, scandals, identity. 暴露身分 (blow one's cover), 暴露問題 (expose problems), 暴露在陽光下 (exposed to sunlight, literal). Different from 揭露 (more journalistic 'reveal/expose') and 透露 (deliberately disclose, neutral).

examples.chinese: 這次危機暴露了管理上的問題。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì wéijī bàolùle guǎnlǐ shàng de wèntí.
examples.english: This crisis exposed problems in management.

semanticNote: Originally a photography term — exposing film to light. Modern dominant sense: media exposure, public disclosure of something previously private. 醜聞被曝光 (the scandal was exposed), 曝光率 (exposure rate, marketing). Sister to 暴露 but with media/publicity flavor. Heteronym alert: 曝 read pù means 'to sun-dry' (曝曬 = scorch in the sun).

examples.chinese: 那位明星的婚訊被媒體曝光了。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi míngxīng de hūnxùn bèi méitǐ bàoguāng le.
examples.english: That celebrity's marriage news was leaked by the media.

semanticNote: Sudden outbreak — wars (戰爭爆發), epidemics (疫情爆發), volcanos, scandals, emotions (情緒爆發). The action is sudden and forceful, often coming after pressure builds up. Compare to 爆炸 (literal explosion) — 爆發 is broader and often metaphorical/event-scale.

examples.chinese: 兩國之間爆發了戰爭。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng guó zhī jiān bàofāle zhànzhēng.
examples.english: War broke out between the two countries.

semanticNote: Literal explosion — bombs, gas leaks, pressure cookers. Both verb and noun. Figurative: 信息爆炸 (information explosion), 人口爆炸 (population explosion). Also colloquial: 我頭都要爆炸了 (my head is about to explode — from stress). 爆炸性新聞 = bombshell news.

examples.chinese: 工廠發生了大爆炸。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchǎng fāshēngle dà bàozhà.
examples.english: A massive explosion occurred at the factory.

semanticNote: Strong moral condemnation — describes a person, action, or scheme that is unprincipled and underhanded. 卑鄙的手段 (despicable methods), 卑鄙小人 (a despicable scoundrel). One of the harsher insults in Mandarin. Compare to 無恥 (shameless) and 下流 (vulgar/lewd) — 卑鄙 emphasizes lack of moral principle.

examples.chinese: 他用卑鄙的手段陷害同事。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng bēibǐ de shǒuduàn xiànhài tóngshì.
examples.english: He used despicable means to frame his colleague.

semanticNote: Deep, dignified sorrow — heavier than 難過 (sad), more reflective than 痛苦 (suffering). Often used for tragic situations or existential reflections: 人生的悲哀 (the sorrow of life). Sometimes carries a touch of pity or resignation: 真是悲哀 = how sad / how pitiful. Literary register.

examples.chinese: 她的眼神充滿了悲哀。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yǎnshén chōngmǎnle bēi'āi.
examples.english: Her eyes were full of sorrow.

semanticNote: Used for genuinely tragic, heart-wrenching situations — wars, accidents, refugee plight, devastating personal stories. 悲慘的命運 (tragic fate), 悲慘世界 (Les Misérables — yes, that's the Chinese title). Stronger and more dramatic than 悲哀 — 悲慘 implies external suffering, not just emotional sadness.

examples.chinese: 戰爭給人民帶來悲慘的生活。
examples.pinyin: Zhànzhēng gěi rénmín dàiláile bēicǎn de shēnghuó.
examples.english: War brought a miserable life to the people.

semanticNote: The North Pole and the Arctic region. 北極熊 = polar bear, 北極星 = North Star. Pair with 南極 (South Pole/Antarctic). Often appears in geography, climate change discussions, and nature documentaries.

examples.chinese: 北極的冰層正在融化。
examples.pinyin: Běijí de bīngcéng zhèngzài rónghuà.
examples.english: The Arctic ice is melting.

semanticNote: The shell of a seashell. Beachy, evocative word. 撿貝殼 = collect shells. The character 貝 itself is interesting — it depicts a cowrie shell, which was used as ancient money, hence its appearance in characters relating to wealth (財, 貴, 賺).

examples.chinese: 孩子們在沙灘上撿貝殼。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài shātān shàng jiǎn bèiké.
examples.english: The kids collected seashells on the beach.

semanticNote: Tech vocab: data backup. Both noun (a backup) and verb (to back up). 雲端備份 (cloud backup), 自動備份 (automatic backup). Modern essential word — anyone who's lost a hard drive learns this fast.

examples.chinese: 記得每週備份重要文件。
examples.pinyin: Jìde měi zhōu bèifèn zhòngyào wénjiàn.
examples.english: Remember to back up important files weekly.

semanticNote: Two contexts: (1) a memo / note-to-self (the Notes app on your phone is often called 備忘錄); (2) formal/diplomatic memorandum between organizations or governments — 簽署備忘錄 (sign a memorandum). The everyday phone-app sense dominates in casual speech now.

examples.chinese: 我把待辦事項記在備忘錄裡。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ dàibàn shìxiàng jì zài bèiwànglù lǐ.
examples.english: I keep my to-dos in the memo app.

semanticNote: Strong word — to betray someone or something you owed loyalty to: a friend, country, cause, marriage. 背叛朋友 (betray a friend), 背叛祖國 (betray one's country). Compare to 出賣 (sell out — emphasizes mercenary motive). 背叛 emphasizes the broken trust, regardless of motive.

examples.chinese: 他被最好的朋友背叛了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi zuì hǎo de péngyǒu bèipàn le.
examples.english: He was betrayed by his best friend.

semanticNote: To memorize something and recite it back — typically poems, classical texts, scripture, multiplication tables. Quintessential Chinese-school activity (背誦古詩 = memorize and recite classical poetry). Compare to 背 alone (also 'memorize/recite', same root) — 背誦 is the formal full word.

examples.chinese: 學生們在背誦唐詩。
examples.pinyin: Xuéshēngmen zài bèisòng Táng shī.
examples.english: The students are reciting Tang dynasty poems.

semanticNote: Two main uses: (1) personality / attitude — passive (被動的態度 = passive attitude), often implying lack of initiative; (2) grammatical passive voice (被動語態). The personality sense is mildly negative — Chinese culture generally values being 主動 (proactive). Compare to 消極 (negative/inactive) which is harsher.

examples.chinese: 他在感情中總是很被動。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gǎnqíng zhōng zǒngshì hěn bèidòng.
examples.english: He's always passive in relationships.

semanticNote: Legal term: the person being sued or charged. Pair with 原告 (plaintiff). Court-and-news vocabulary. 被告人 = defendant (slightly fuller form, criminal context).

examples.chinese: 被告否認所有指控。
examples.pinyin: Bèigào fǒurèn suǒyǒu zhǐkòng.
examples.english: The defendant denied all charges.

semanticNote: To run around busily — usually with a tone of weariness or struggle. 為生活奔波 (toil for one's livelihood), 四處奔波 (rush around all over). Carries emotional weight: this is the word for tired hustle, the parent working three jobs, the salesperson on the road. Compare to 忙 (just 'busy', neutral).

examples.chinese: 他每天為了工作四處奔波。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān wèile gōngzuò sìchù bēnbō.
examples.english: He rushes around every day for work.

semanticNote: To run/speed at high pace — horses (馬在草原上奔馳), cars on highways, even time figuratively (時光奔馳). Also the official Chinese name for Mercedes-Benz — chosen because it sounds like 'Benz' AND means 'galloping speed.' One of the great brand-name translations into Chinese.

examples.chinese: 駿馬在草原上奔馳。
examples.pinyin: Jùnmǎ zài cǎoyuán shàng bēnchí.
examples.english: The fine horses galloped across the grasslands.

semanticNote: Instinct — innate, biological. 本能反應 (instinctive reaction), 求生本能 (survival instinct), 母性本能 (maternal instinct). Used in psychology, biology, and casual speech alike. Compare to 直覺 (intuition — also gut-level but more cognitive than purely biological).

examples.chinese: 她出於母愛的本能保護孩子。
examples.pinyin: Tā chū yú mǔ'ài de běnnéng bǎohù háizi.
examples.english: Out of maternal instinct she protected her child.

semanticNote: The starting money or assets you have to work with — for business, investments, or even life. 做生意需要本錢 (you need capital to do business). Figurative use: 年輕就是本錢 (youth itself is capital). Down-to-earth, direct word — more colloquial than 資本 (capital, formal/economics).

examples.chinese: 我沒有足夠的本錢開店。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu zúgòu de běnqián kāidiàn.
examples.english: I don't have enough capital to open a shop.

semanticNote: Formal self-reference — 'I, the undersigned' / 'the person themselves.' Used in official documents, when emphasizing self vs. proxy (你必須本人到場 = you must come in person), or in formal speech. Slightly stilted in casual conversation. Sometimes used jokingly when speaking with mock-formality about oneself.

examples.chinese: 取件需要本人帶證件。
examples.pinyin: Qǔ jiàn xūyào běnrén dài zhèngjiàn.
examples.english: You need to come pick it up in person with ID.

semanticNote: '(The thing) itself' — used to focus on something's intrinsic nature apart from circumstances or appearances. 問題本身 (the problem itself), 這件事本身 (this matter in and of itself). Common in analytical writing and argument: 'X itself isn't the issue, but...' Different from 自己 (one's own self, personal pronoun).

examples.chinese: 這個想法本身沒有問題。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiǎngfǎ běnshēn méiyǒu wèntí.
examples.english: The idea itself is fine.

english: ability; skill; what one is capable of
semanticNote: Practical skill / what someone can actually do. Colloquial and proud — 真有本事 (truly skilled / a real talent). Often used in challenges or boasts: 有本事你就試試 (if you're so capable, try it). Different from 能力 (ability, more formal/abstract). 本事 implies demonstrated, practical chops.

examples.chinese: 他真有本事，一個月就學會了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhēn yǒu běnshi, yí ge yuè jiù xuéhuì le.
examples.english: He's really got skills — learned it in a month.

semanticNote: Clumsy in body or in skill — physically awkward, or unrefined in technique. Can describe a person, movement, writing, or technique. 笨拙的動作 (clumsy movements), 笨拙的安慰 (an awkward attempt at comfort). Not necessarily harsh — can be tender (a clumsy but sincere effort).

examples.chinese: 他笨拙地表達了感謝。
examples.pinyin: Tā bènzhuō de biǎodále gǎnxiè.
examples.english: He awkwardly expressed his thanks.

semanticNote: Sudden total collapse — physical (a building, an empire, an economy) or psychological (a person's mental state). 精神崩潰 (mental breakdown), 系統崩潰 (system crash). Also colloquial for 'I'm losing it' / 'I'm freaking out': 我快崩潰了. Modern internet/youth speech uses it constantly to mean 'overwhelmed.'

examples.chinese: 工作壓力大到讓我快崩潰了。
examples.pinyin: Gōngzuò yālì dà dào ràng wǒ kuài bēngkuì le.
examples.english: The work stress is so much I'm about to break down.

english: need not; don't need to (colloquial contraction)
semanticNote: A character contraction of 不用 (no need / don't need). The character itself stacks 不 on 用 — visual etymology. Very colloquial, especially Beijing-flavored: 甭客氣 (no need to be polite), 甭說了 (no need to say it / drop it). Less common in Taiwan, where 不用 dominates. Hearing 甭 marks someone as Northern.

examples.chinese: 這事兒甭提了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shìr béng tí le.
examples.english: Don't even bring this up.

semanticNote: Sudden bursting forth of something contained — energy, passion, ideas, sparks. 迸發出火花 (sparks burst forth), 靈感迸發 (inspiration bursts forth). Literary/dramatic register, often used to describe creative or emotional moments. Different from 爆發 (eruption of events) — 迸發 emphasizes the springing-out moment.

examples.chinese: 討論中迸發出許多新想法。
examples.pinyin: Tǎolùn zhōng bèngfā chū xǔduō xīn xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: Many new ideas burst forth during the discussion.

semanticNote: Lighter, springier jump — a kid hopping, a frog, a basketball bouncing. Compare to 跳 (jump, broader and more general) — 蹦 is more energetic and bouncy. 蹦蹦跳跳 = bouncing and jumping (cute reduplication for kids' movement). 蹦極 = bungee jumping.

examples.chinese: 小孩高興得蹦了起來。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎohái gāoxìng de bèngle qǐlái.
examples.english: The child jumped up with joy.

semanticNote: To pressure someone into doing something against their will — through threats, circumstances, or persistent demands. Negative. 被迫 = be forced to (very common passive form). Compare to 強迫 (force, similar) and 迫使 (compel, more formal). 逼迫 emphasizes the squeezing pressure.

examples.chinese: 父母不應該逼迫孩子做不想做的事。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ bù yīnggāi bīpò háizi zuò bù xiǎng zuò de shì.
examples.english: Parents shouldn't force kids to do things they don't want to.

semanticNote: Snot — exactly what it sounds like. 流鼻涕 = runny nose (the everyday cold-symptom phrase). 擦鼻涕 = wipe your nose. Earthy, common word — not gross, just everyday body vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 他感冒了，一直流鼻涕。
examples.pinyin: Tā gǎnmào le, yìzhí liú bítì.
examples.english: He has a cold and his nose keeps running.

semanticNote: 打個比方 = 'let me give you an example' / 'as an analogy' — extremely common spoken phrase used to introduce an illustration. Less formal than 比喻. Both noun and verb-like usage. 比方說 = 'for instance.'

examples.chinese: 打個比方,學語言就像跑馬拉松。
examples.pinyin: Dǎ ge bǐfang, xué yǔyán jiù xiàng pǎo mǎlāsōng.
examples.english: For example — learning a language is like running a marathon.

semanticNote: The literary device — metaphor or simile (Chinese doesn't strictly distinguish). Used in literary analysis: 用比喻的手法 (using metaphorical technique). More formal than 比方 — 比喻 is the textbook term for figurative language.

examples.chinese: 作者用海洋比喻人生的廣闊。
examples.pinyin: Zuòzhě yòng hǎiyáng bǐyù rénshēng de guǎngkuò.
examples.english: The author uses the ocean as a metaphor for the vastness of life.

semanticNote: Two senses: (1) physics/chemistry — specific gravity; (2) more commonly, the proportion or weight (importance) of something within a whole — 占很大比重 = takes up a large proportion. Common in statistics, economics, and analytical writing.

examples.chinese: 服務業在經濟中的比重越來越大。
examples.pinyin: Fúwùyè zài jīngjì zhōng de bǐzhòng yuèláiyuè dà.
examples.english: The service sector's share of the economy is growing.

semanticNote: To hold someone or something in contempt. Stronger than 看不起 (look down on, more colloquial). 鄙視的眼神 (a contemptuous look). Often used in moral judgments — looking down on cheaters, cowards, or those who betray principles.

examples.chinese: 我鄙視那種出賣朋友的行為。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǐshì nà zhǒng chūmài péngyǒu de xíngwéi.
examples.english: I despise that kind of friend-selling-out behavior.

semanticNote: Two flavors: (1) physically blocked / obstructed — 鼻子閉塞 (stuffed-up nose), 交通閉塞 (traffic jammed); (2) figuratively isolated and uninformed — 信息閉塞 (cut off from information), 思想閉塞 (close-minded). Often used to describe remote, undeveloped areas.

examples.chinese: 那個山村非常閉塞,信息不通。
examples.pinyin: Nà ge shāncūn fēicháng bìsè, xìnxī bùtōng.
examples.english: That mountain village is very isolated, cut off from the world.

semanticNote: A systemic flaw or deep-seated problem — in a system, organization, or society. Suggests something chronic and harmful. 制度的弊病 (institutional flaws). Compare to 缺點 (shortcoming, milder, individual-scale) and 弊端 (sister-word, used for malpractice/abuse).

examples.chinese: 這個制度有許多弊病需要改革。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge zhìdù yǒu xǔduō bìbìng xūyào gǎigé.
examples.english: This system has many flaws that need reform.

semanticNote: Specific corrupt or harmful practices within a system. More concrete than 弊病 — 弊端 are the actual abuses (bribery, fraud, exploitation), while 弊病 is the general malady. 揭露弊端 = expose the abuses. Common in news exposés.

examples.chinese: 他揭露了公司內部的弊端。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiēlùle gōngsī nèibù de bìduān.
examples.english: He exposed the company's internal abuses.

semanticNote: The arm — more formal/literary than the everyday 胳膊 (which is the spoken word for arm). 臂 appears in compounds: 手臂 (arm), 臂膀 (arm/upper arm), 一臂之力 (a helping hand, literally 'the strength of one arm'). Standalone usage is largely literary.

examples.chinese: 他舉起手臂打招呼。
examples.pinyin: Tā jǔ qǐ shǒubì dǎzhāohu.
examples.english: He raised his arm in greeting.

semanticNote: The frontier region of a country — borderlands, often distant and culturally distinct from the heartland. Carries a romantic/heroic flavor in Chinese literature: pioneers, soldiers, ethnic minority regions. 戍守邊疆 (guard the frontier). Distinguish from 邊界 (border line) and 邊境 (border zone, more administrative).

examples.chinese: 他在邊疆服役了十年。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài biānjiāng fúyìle shí nián.
examples.english: He served in the borderlands for ten years.

semanticNote: The actual line of a border — geographic, political, or abstract (邊界感 = sense of personal boundaries, a modern psychology buzzword). 跨越邊界 = cross the boundary. More precise than 邊境 (border zone). Modern relationship-and-therapy talk has popularized the abstract sense.

examples.chinese: 我們需要尊重彼此的邊界。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào zūnzhòng bǐcǐ de biānjiè.
examples.english: We need to respect each other's boundaries.

semanticNote: The border area — slightly thicker than 邊界 (a line). The zone right by a national border, with associated administrative/military meaning. 邊境管制 (border control), 邊境衝突 (border conflict). Compare 邊疆 (frontier, more vast and romantic).

examples.chinese: 兩國在邊境發生了衝突。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng guó zài biānjìng fāshēngle chōngtū.
examples.english: The two countries had a clash at the border.

semanticNote: The edge of something — a table, a cliff, society. Powerful figurative use: 在崩潰的邊緣 (on the verge of collapse), 邊緣人 (a marginalized person / a wallflower). Modern psychology / sociology has made this word ubiquitous.

examples.chinese: 他覺得自己是社會的邊緣人。
examples.pinyin: Tā juéde zìjǐ shì shèhuì de biānyuán rén.
examples.english: He feels like he's on the margins of society.

semanticNote: Physical: weaving textiles, knitting sweaters, braiding hair. Figurative: 編織夢想 (weave dreams), 編織謊言 (weave lies). Particularly evocative when used metaphorically — implies intricate, deliberate construction.

examples.chinese: 奶奶在編織毛衣。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai zài biānzhī máoyī.
examples.english: Grandma is knitting a sweater.

semanticNote: Originally to whip a horse onward. Modern use: figurative — to motivate or push someone (or oneself) toward improvement. Often positive: 鞭策自己 (push oneself), 老師的鞭策 (the teacher's prodding). Has a slightly intense/disciplined flavor.

examples.chinese: 老師的話一直鞭策著我前進。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī de huà yìzhí biāncèzhe wǒ qiánjìn.
examples.english: My teacher's words have always spurred me forward.

semanticNote: To talk down / make someone or something seem less than they are. 貶低別人 (belittle others). Always negative — implies unfairness or jealousy. Compare to 批評 (criticize, can be constructive) — 貶低 is purely deflating.

examples.chinese: 他總是貶低同事的工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì biǎndī tóngshì de gōngzuò.
examples.english: He's always belittling his coworkers' work.

semanticNote: The 'derogatory sense' of a word — a linguistic concept. 帶有貶義 (has a derogatory connotation), 貶義詞 (derogatory word). Pair with 褒義 (commendatory/positive sense). Useful when explaining or discussing word choice.

examples.chinese: "狡猾"這個詞帶有貶義。
examples.pinyin: "Jiǎohuá" zhè ge cí dài yǒu biǎnyì.
examples.english: The word "cunning" has a derogatory connotation.

semanticNote: Flat in shape — a flat tire (扁了的輪胎), flat box, flattened object. 壓扁 = squash flat. Also colloquial: 揍扁你 = beat you flat / beat you up (somewhat playful threat).

examples.chinese: 輪胎扁了,需要打氣。
examples.pinyin: Lúntāi biǎn le, xūyào dǎqì.
examples.english: The tire is flat, needs air.

semanticNote: An unexpected and usually unfortunate event — a sudden upheaval in someone's life. Death, illness, accident, sudden divorce. 家庭變故 (family upheaval). Heavier and more dramatic than 意外 (accident/surprise). News and biographical writing.

examples.chinese: 他經歷了家庭變故,變得沉默。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīnglìle jiātíng biàngù, biànde chénmò.
examples.english: After family tragedies, he became withdrawn.

semanticNote: Gradual large-scale change — historical, cultural, environmental, demographic. 時代變遷 (changes of the era), 城市的變遷 (urban transformation). Reflective and sweeping in flavor. Common in essays, documentaries, and historical writing.

examples.chinese: 這座城市見證了時代的變遷。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì jiànzhèngle shídài de biànqiān.
examples.english: This city has witnessed the changes of the era.

semanticNote: Two senses: (1) food spoilage — 食物變質 (food has gone bad); (2) deterioration of character or nature — 友誼變質 (the friendship turned sour), 革命變質 (the revolution betrayed its ideals). The metaphorical use is powerful — implies fundamental corruption, not just decline.

examples.chinese: 這牛奶已經變質了,別喝。
examples.pinyin: Zhè niúnǎi yǐjīng biànzhì le, bié hē.
examples.english: This milk has gone bad — don't drink it.

semanticNote: Convenient — slightly more formal than 方便 (which is the everyday word). 便利商店 = convenience store (one of the most common compound uses, especially in Taiwan where they're a way of life). 便利性 = convenience as a quality.

examples.chinese: 網購給生活帶來很多便利。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnggòu gěi shēnghuó dàilái hěn duō biànlì.
examples.english: Online shopping brings lots of convenience to life.

semanticNote: A short informal note — a sticky note, a quick scrawled message left for someone. 留個便條 = leave a note. Pre-smartphone communication; less common in casual modern speech but still used.

examples.chinese: 我在桌上留了便條給你。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài zhuō shàng liúle biàntiáo gěi nǐ.
examples.english: I left a note for you on the desk.

semanticNote: 'Convenient for / easy to do X' — used to describe how a design or arrangement facilitates an action. 便於攜帶 (easy to carry), 便於閱讀 (easy to read). Formal and analytical — common in product descriptions, instructions, and explanations.

examples.chinese: 這個包裝設計便於攜帶。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge bāozhuāng shèjì biànyú xiédài.
examples.english: This package design is easy to carry.

english: to be found everywhere; spread all over
semanticNote: To be widely distributed / found everywhere across an area. 分店遍布全國 (branches all over the country), 遍布世界 (around the world). Suggests comprehensive coverage. Common in business and geographic descriptions.

examples.chinese: 他的客戶遍布世界各地。
examples.pinyin: Tā de kèhù biànbù shìjiè gèdì.
examples.english: His clients are spread all over the world.

semanticNote: To identify by careful examination — distinguishing one thing from another similar things. 辨認筆跡 (identify handwriting), 辨認嫌犯 (identify a suspect). Compare to 認 (recognize, simpler) — 辨認 implies effortful identification, often forensic or investigative.

examples.chinese: 目擊者辨認出了犯人。
examples.pinyin: Mùjízhě biànrènchūle fànrén.
examples.english: The witness identified the perpetrator.

semanticNote: To argue in someone's defense — primarily in legal contexts (辯護律師 = defense lawyer), but also in everyday situations (為自己辯護 = defend oneself in argument). Implies organized argument, not just contradiction.

examples.chinese: 律師為被告辯護。
examples.pinyin: Lǜshī wèi bèigào biànhù.
examples.english: The lawyer defends the defendant.

semanticNote: To explain oneself in defense, often when accused of something. Has a slightly defensive tone — sometimes implies excuse-making. 不要為自己辯解 (don't make excuses for yourself). Compare to 解釋 (explain, neutral) — 辯解 implies a charge has been made.

examples.chinese: 他試圖為自己的錯誤辯解。
examples.pinyin: Tā shìtú wèi zìjǐ de cuòwù biànjiě.
examples.english: He tried to justify his mistake.

semanticNote: Philosophical term, primarily — dialectical (Hegel/Marx). 辯證法 = dialectics, 辯證唯物主義 = dialectical materialism. In casual speech 辯證地看 = look at it dialectically (i.e., consider both sides). Heavy academic register; mostly philosophy and politics.

examples.chinese: 我們應該辯證地看待這個問題。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi biànzhèng de kàndài zhè ge wèntí.
examples.english: We should look at this issue dialectically.

semanticNote: A hair braid. 紮辮子 = tie braids. Idiom: 抓辮子 = (figurative) catch someone's mistake / find a weakness to exploit (literally 'grab the pigtail'). Children-and-hairstyle vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 小女孩有兩條長長的辮子。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo nǚhái yǒu liǎng tiáo chángcháng de biànzi.
examples.english: The little girl has two long braids.

semanticNote: Scientific specimen — a butterfly mounted in a case, a tissue sample for analysis. Also figurative: 治標不治本 = treat the symptoms, not the root cause (the 標 is the surface/symptom, 本 is the root). Medical, biological, and scientific contexts.

examples.chinese: 博物館展出了許多昆蟲標本。
examples.pinyin: Bówùguǎn zhǎnchūle xǔduō kūnchóng biāoběn.
examples.english: The museum displayed many insect specimens.

semanticNote: A mark or label — both physical (marking on a map, package, document) and digital (tagging in apps). 做標記 = make a mark. In tech: tag/label data. The word doubles as both noun and verb.

examples.chinese: 請在重要的地方做標記。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhòngyào de dìfāng zuò biāojì.
examples.english: Please mark the important parts.

semanticNote: Title of an article, headline of news, heading of a section. 標題黨 = clickbait artists (literally 'title party' — those who write misleading sensational titles). Modern internet use makes this word ubiquitous.

examples.chinese: 這篇文章的標題很吸引人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng de biāotí hěn xīyǐn rén.
examples.english: This article's title is very catchy.

english: to decide by vote; vote on
semanticNote: To put something to a vote — formal/procedural. 舉手表決 (vote by raising hands), 表決通過 (passed by vote). Used in meetings, councils, parliaments. Different from 投票 (cast a vote, individual action) — 表決 is the group decision-making process.

examples.chinese: 委員會將對這個提案進行表決。
examples.pinyin: Wěiyuánhuì jiāng duì zhè ge tí'àn jìnxíng biǎojué.
examples.english: The committee will vote on this proposal.

english: to declare one's stance; make one's position known
semanticNote: Particularly common in political and workplace contexts — to publicly state where you stand on an issue. 不肯表態 (refuse to take a position). Carries social weight: refusing to 表態 can be read as cowardly or strategically slick.

examples.chinese: 老闆遲遲不表態。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn chíchí bù biǎotài.
examples.english: The boss is dragging his feet on declaring his position.

semanticNote: Public commendation — usually formal recognition by an institution. 表彰大會 (commendation meeting), 表彰先進 (commend the outstanding). Stronger and more formal than 表揚 (praise, broader). Often involves certificates, awards, public ceremonies.

examples.chinese: 公司表彰了優秀員工。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī biǎozhāngle yōuxiù yuángōng.
examples.english: The company commended outstanding employees.

semanticNote: To hold something in — physically (憋尿 = hold pee, 憋氣 = hold breath) or emotionally (憋著一肚子氣 = bottling up anger). 憋了好久 = held it in for a long time. Earthy, vivid word — implies pressure building up. Also 憋屈 = the feeling of being suppressed/stifled.

examples.chinese: 他憋了一肚子話想說。
examples.pinyin: Tā biēle yí dùzi huà xiǎng shuō.
examples.english: He's been holding back a bellyful of things to say.

semanticNote: A standalone luxury house — villa, mansion. Implies wealth and detached single-family home (rare and aspirational in dense Chinese cities where most people live in apartments). 海邊別墅 = seaside villa.

examples.chinese: 他在郊區買了一棟別墅。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jiāoqū mǎile yí dòng biéshù.
examples.english: He bought a villa in the suburbs.

semanticNote: Stylishly different — used positively for design, clothing, decor, restaurants. 很別致的小店 (a unique little shop). Compliments that something stands out tastefully (vs. just being weird). Aesthetic word.

examples.chinese: 她的穿著很別致。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chuānzhuó hěn biézhì.
examples.english: Her style of dress is uniquely stylish.

semanticNote: A wonderfully Chinese word with several flavors: (1) physically awkward / not fitting right (這姿勢很彆扭 = this posture feels awkward); (2) language that doesn't flow naturally (翻譯得很彆扭 = the translation reads awkwardly); (3) interpersonal tension / sulky / passive-aggressive (鬧彆扭 = act sulky, give the silent treatment, especially between couples or family). The third sense is very vivid in spoken Mandarin.

examples.chinese: 她在跟男朋友鬧彆扭。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gēn nán péngyǒu nào bièniu.
examples.english: She's having a sulky tiff with her boyfriend.

english: on the verge of; close to (a critical point)
semanticNote: To be on the brink of — usually negative outcomes. 瀕臨絕種 (on the verge of extinction), 瀕臨破產 (close to bankruptcy), 瀕臨崩潰 (on the verge of collapse). Formal, weighty word for critical thresholds.

examples.chinese: 這種動物已經瀕臨絕種。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng dòngwù yǐjīng bīnlín juézhǒng.
examples.english: This animal is now on the brink of extinction.

semanticNote: Hail. 下冰雹 = hail is falling. Weather vocabulary. 雹子 alone is the more colloquial form.

examples.chinese: 昨天下了冰雹,把車打凹了。
examples.pinyin: Zuótiān xiàle bīngbáo, bǎ chē dǎ āole.
examples.english: It hailed yesterday and dented the car.

semanticNote: The third of the ten Heavenly Stems (天干: 甲乙丙丁...). Used in traditional grading (甲乙丙丁 = A B C D), in Chinese astrology, and as 'Party C' / 'Person C' in legal documents alongside 甲 (Party A) and 乙 (Party B). Also 丙級 = grade C.

examples.chinese: 合同分為甲方、乙方、丙方。
examples.pinyin: Hétóng fēnwéi jiǎfāng, yǐfāng, bǐngfāng.
examples.english: The contract distinguishes Party A, Party B, and Party C.

semanticNote: More formal version of 不是 — 'is not' / 'is by no means.' Used in writing and formal speech to refute or correct a misconception. 並非如此 (it's not like that), 並非偶然 (no coincidence). 並 here adds emphasis. Common in essays, news, and analytical writing.

examples.chinese: 成功並非偶然。
examples.pinyin: Chénggōng bìngfēi ǒurán.
examples.english: Success is not a coincidence.

english: to stand side by side; be juxtaposed
semanticNote: Two or more things placed on equal footing — sports (並列第一 = tied for first), grammar (並列關係 = parallel/coordinate relationship), arrangement (並列在一起 = placed side by side). Implies equal status.

examples.chinese: 兩位選手並列冠軍。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng wèi xuǎnshǒu bìngliè guànjūn.
examples.english: The two contestants tied for the championship.

english: to dial; allocate; flip / push aside
semanticNote: Range of physical 'flicking' actions: dial a phone (撥電話 — though increasingly old-school as no one dials anymore), allocate funds (撥款 = allocate funding), push something aside with a finger (撥開頭髮 = push hair aside). Also 撥動心弦 = pluck at the heartstrings.

examples.chinese: 政府撥款支持教育。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ bōkuǎn zhīchí jiàoyù.
examples.english: The government allocated funds to support education.

semanticNote: Ocean/water waves — concrete and visual. Compare to 波濤 (massive billows, more literary) and 浪 alone (also wave, more colloquial). 波浪線 = wavy line. Standard word for everyday waves on water.

examples.chinese: 海面的波浪很大。
examples.pinyin: Hǎimiàn de bōlàng hěn dà.
examples.english: The waves on the sea are big.

semanticNote: Massive, dramatic waves — literary and powerful. 波濤洶湧 = surging waves (set phrase, used both literally for storms and figuratively for tumultuous events/emotions). Reach for 波濤 when you want emotional grandeur; everyday waves are 波浪.

examples.chinese: 暴風雨中,海上波濤洶湧。
examples.pinyin: Bàofēngyǔ zhōng, hǎi shàng bōtāo xiōngyǒng.
examples.english: In the storm, the sea was raging with huge waves.

semanticNote: Marxist-flavored term for economic exploitation — taking surplus labor value from workers. 剝削勞工 (exploit workers). The character 剝 alone (read bāo) means to peel — extending to figurative 'stripping' someone of value. Loaded political word in mainland press; used more loosely in Taiwan / overseas.

examples.chinese: 老闆剝削員工的勞動成果。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn bōxuē yuángōng de láodòng chéngguǒ.
examples.english: The boss exploits the fruits of the workers' labor.

semanticNote: Literally to scatter seeds for planting. Common metaphor: 播種希望 (sow seeds of hope), 春天播種,秋天收穫 (sow in spring, reap in autumn — also figurative for cause and effect). Agricultural foundation, philosophical extension.

examples.chinese: 農夫春天播種,秋天收成。
examples.pinyin: Nóngfū chūntiān bōzhǒng, qiūtiān shōuchéng.
examples.english: Farmers sow in spring and harvest in autumn.

semanticNote: Specifically the wife of one's father's older brother — Chinese kinship is precise. 伯父 = father's older brother, 伯母 = his wife. Also commonly used as a polite way to address an older woman roughly your mother's age, even if unrelated (like calling someone 'auntie').

examples.chinese: 伯母,您好!
examples.pinyin: Bómǔ, nín hǎo!
examples.english: Hello, Auntie!

semanticNote: 'Broad and deep' — describes culture, philosophy, knowledge, wisdom that has both wide scope and deep substance. Almost always used to describe Chinese culture itself: 中華文化博大精深. Reverent, often used in formal contexts and cultural pride speech.

examples.chinese: 中華文化博大精深。
examples.pinyin: Zhōnghuá wénhuà bódàjīngshēn.
examples.english: Chinese culture is vast and profound.

semanticNote: A large exhibition or fair — international expos, trade shows, world's fairs. 世界博覽會 = World Expo. 上海世博會 = Shanghai Expo (the famous 2010 one). Formal/event word.

examples.chinese: 上海舉辦了世界博覽會。
examples.pinyin: Shànghǎi jǔbànle Shìjiè bólǎnhuì.
examples.english: Shanghai hosted the World Expo.

semanticNote: Physical struggle — fighting hand-to-hand with someone, or wrestling against waves, illness, fate. 與命運搏鬥 (struggle against fate). More dramatic than 打架 (fight), heavier than 鬥爭 (struggle, more abstract). Often used metaphorically for life challenges.

examples.chinese: 他與病魔搏鬥了三年。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǔ bìngmó bódòule sān nián.
examples.english: He battled the illness for three years.

semanticNote: Weak in capacity or substance — typically applied to abstract qualities: 意志薄弱 (weak willpower), 基礎薄弱 (weak foundation), 證據薄弱 (weak evidence). Different from 弱 (just 'weak', physical) — 薄弱 implies thinness/insufficiency in something that should be solid.

examples.chinese: 他的數學基礎比較薄弱。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shùxué jīchǔ bǐjiào bóruò.
examples.english: His math foundation is rather weak.

semanticNote: To pay back what was lost — money compensation for damage, or making up for time/attention not given (補償你 = make it up to you). Both legal/financial and emotional contexts. Common in insurance, lawsuits, and relationship apologies.

examples.chinese: 公司會補償你的損失。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī huì bǔcháng nǐ de sǔnshī.
examples.english: The company will compensate you for the loss.

semanticNote: To fix a mistake or salvage a bad situation before it gets worse. 為時已晚,無法補救 (it's too late, can't be remedied). Carries the sense of damage control. Compare to 修復 (repair, more physical).

examples.chinese: 事情還來得及補救。
examples.pinyin: Shìqíng hái láidejí bǔjiù.
examples.english: There's still time to fix this.

semanticNote: A subsidy — government, employer, or family financial support. 政府補貼 (government subsidy), 房屋補貼 (housing allowance). Also as verb: to subsidize. Common in policy and HR contexts.

examples.chinese: 政府給農民提供補貼。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ gěi nóngmín tígōng bǔtiē.
examples.english: The government provides subsidies to farmers.

semanticNote: To catch — animals (捕捉野生動物), criminals, but most beautifully abstract: 捕捉靈感 (capture inspiration), 捕捉瞬間 (capture the moment, common in photography). The metaphorical use is loved by writers.

examples.chinese: 攝影師擅長捕捉精彩瞬間。
examples.pinyin: Shèyǐngshī shàncháng bǔzhuō jīngcǎi shùnjiān.
examples.english: The photographer is skilled at capturing wonderful moments.

semanticNote: Breastfeeding. 哺乳期 (lactation period), 哺乳動物 (mammals — literally 'suckling animals'). Medical and biological context.

examples.chinese: 她正在哺乳期。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài bǔrǔqī.
examples.english: She's currently in the breastfeeding period.

english: have no alternative; do something reluctantly
semanticNote: 'No choice but to' — used when explaining a reluctant action forced by circumstances. 不得已的選擇 (a forced choice), 萬不得已 (only as a very last resort). Defensive / explanatory tone — implies regret about the necessity.

examples.chinese: 我也是不得已才這麼做的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yě shì bùdéyǐ cái zhème zuò de.
examples.english: I only did this because I had no other choice.

english: might as well; there's no harm in
semanticNote: Suggests trying something as a reasonable option — 'might as well,' 'why not,' 'no harm in doing X.' Always followed by a verb phrase: 不妨試試 (might as well give it a try), 不妨直說 (no harm in saying it directly). Slightly softer and more tentative than 可以 (can/may). Has a mildly encouraging tone — the speaker is nudging someone toward an action without pressure. Formal enough to appear in writing but common in spoken Mandarin too.

examples.chinese: 你不妨去問問他，也許他知道。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bùfáng qù wènwen tā, yěxǔ tā zhīdào.
examples.english: Why not go ask him — maybe he knows.

examples.chinese: 這個方法不妨試試，反正沒有損失。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fāngfǎ bùfáng shìshì, fǎnzhèng méiyǒu sǔnshī.
examples.english: Might as well try this method — nothing to lose anyway.

english: you flatter me; I don't deserve such praise
semanticNote: Polite humility phrase — a deflection of praise, like 'oh, you flatter me' or 'I'm not worthy.' Used when complimented or addressed too respectfully. Cultural muscle: Chinese speakers are expected to deflect praise. Particularly common from elders or in formal interactions.

examples.chinese: 您過獎了,不敢當。
examples.pinyin: Nín guòjiǎng le, bùgǎndāng.
examples.english: You praise me too much — I don't deserve it.

semanticNote: To act without regard for something — usually consequences, others' feelings, or rules. 不顧後果 (regardless of consequences), 不顧一切 (no matter what), 不顧別人感受 (without regard for others' feelings). Often carries criticism — implies recklessness or selfishness.

examples.chinese: 他不顧家人的反對,堅持出國。
examples.pinyin: Tā búgù jiārén de fǎnduì, jiānchí chūguó.
examples.english: He insisted on going abroad despite his family's objections.

english: can't help but; can't refrain from
semanticNote: To be unable to hold back a reaction — laughter, tears, a thought. 不禁笑了 (couldn't help laughing), 不禁想起 (can't help but think of). Slightly literary — implies an involuntary, often emotional response. Compare to 忍不住 (couldn't resist, more colloquial).

examples.chinese: 看到那個場景,我不禁掉下了眼淚。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào nà ge chǎngjǐng, wǒ bùjīn diào xiàle yǎnlèi.
examples.english: Seeing that scene, I couldn't help but shed tears.

semanticNote: Two uses: (1) 'cannot bear' — 不堪重負 (cannot bear the burden), 不堪入目 (unbearable to look at); (2) suffix intensifier — 疲憊不堪 (utterly exhausted), 狼狽不堪 (in a terrible state). The suffix usage is very common and adds 'extremely' to a negative state.

examples.chinese: 工作壓力讓他疲憊不堪。
examples.pinyin: Gōngzuò yālì ràng tā píbèi bùkān.
examples.english: Work pressure has utterly exhausted him.

semanticNote: Literally 'cannot think or discuss it' — something so extraordinary it defies comprehension. Can express genuine awe (a scientific discovery, a miraculous feat) or incredulous disbelief (something outrageous or absurd). In modern spoken Mandarin, often used hyperbolically and positively — like 'unbelievable!' about a great meal or performance. Less formal than written registers suggest; very common in casual speech. Compare to 難以置信 (hard to believe — more about disbelief than awe).

examples.chinese: 他竟然在三天內跑完了一百公里，真是不可思議。
examples.pinyin: Tā jìngrán zài sān tiān nèi pǎowánle yī bǎi gōnglǐ, zhēn shì bùkěsīyì.
examples.english: He actually ran 100 kilometers in three days — absolutely mind-boggling.

examples.chinese: 宇宙的廣大讓人覺得不可思議。
examples.pinyin: Yǔzhòu de guǎngdà ràng rén juéde bùkěsīyì.
examples.english: The vastness of the universe is simply inconceivable.

english: to live up to (the title); deserve to be called
semanticNote: Used to express genuine admiration — 'truly worthy of being called X.' 不愧是冠軍 (truly worthy of being champion), 不愧為老師 (lives up to being a teacher). Praise-flavored. The 愧 (shame) gets negated — 'no shame in being called this.'

examples.chinese: 他不愧是專業選手。
examples.pinyin: Tā búkuì shì zhuānyè xuǎnshǒu.
examples.english: He truly lives up to being a pro athlete.

semanticNote: Storytelling word: 'who would have thought' / 'unexpectedly.' Used to introduce a plot twist or surprising development. 本來計畫得好好的,不料... (We had planned it all out, but unexpectedly...). Common in narrative, news, anecdotes. Compare to 沒想到 (didn't expect, more colloquial).

examples.chinese: 我們本來要出門,不料下起了大雨。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen běnlái yào chūmén, búliào xiàqǐle dàyǔ.
examples.english: We were going to head out, but unexpectedly it started pouring.

semanticNote: 'Unavoidably' / 'inevitably' — usually introducing a feeling or reaction that follows naturally from a situation. 不免擔心 (can't help worrying), 不免有些失望 (inevitably a bit disappointed). Reflective, slightly literary.

examples.chinese: 看到這結果,他不免有些失望。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào zhè jiéguǒ, tā bùmiǎn yǒuxiē shīwàng.
examples.english: Seeing this result, he was inevitably a bit disappointed.

semanticNote: 'Now and then' / 'at frequent intervals.' 不時回頭 (looking back from time to time). Slightly more literary than 經常 (often) or 時不時 (every now and then). Often appears in descriptive narrative writing.

examples.chinese: 她不時看一眼手機。
examples.pinyin: Tā bùshí kàn yì yǎn shǒujī.
examples.english: She glanced at her phone now and then.

semanticNote: To go to extreme lengths — willing to do or sacrifice anything for a goal. 不惜代價 (whatever the cost), 不惜一切 (regardless of all else), 不惜犧牲 (not sparing the sacrifice). Strong commitment word, can be admiring or critical depending on context.

examples.chinese: 他不惜代價追求夢想。
examples.pinyin: Tā bùxī dàijià zhuīqiú mèngxiǎng.
examples.english: He pursues his dream no matter the cost.

semanticNote: Two things at the same level — 'neither above nor below the other.' Used for comparison in skill, quality, performance. 兩人實力不相上下 (the two are evenly matched). Common in sports, competition, debate.

examples.chinese: 兩個品牌的品質不相上下。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng ge pǐnpái de pǐnzhì bùxiāngshàngxià.
examples.english: The two brands' quality is about the same.

semanticNote: Strong colloquial expression of disapproval — 'this is outrageous!' / 'how can you act like this!' 真不像話! is a parental/outraged exclamation when someone has crossed a line. Common in family arguments and indignant complaints. Literally 'not like a [proper] saying' — i.e., beyond reasonable expression.

examples.chinese: 你這樣說真不像話。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhèyàng shuō zhēn búxiànghuà.
examples.english: It's outrageous for you to say that.

english: to disdain; not even worth a glance
semanticNote: To consider something so beneath you that you won't even look. Strong contempt. 對他不屑一顧 (won't even glance at him in disdain). Powerful and slightly cold — implies the person/thing has been judged unworthy of attention.

examples.chinese: 她對這種小事不屑一顧。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhè zhǒng xiǎoshì búxièyígù.
examples.english: She doesn't deign to even glance at such trivial matters.

semanticNote: 'Doesn't need to be said to be understood' — used to introduce something obvious. 結果不言而喻 (the result goes without saying). Common in formal writing and analysis to wrap up a point. Slightly more elegant than 顯而易見 (obvious).

examples.chinese: 他的重要性不言而喻。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zhòngyàoxìng bùyán'éryù.
examples.english: His importance goes without saying.

semanticNote: Same family as 不禁 — describes an involuntary reaction. 不由得笑了 (couldn't help laughing). Slightly more colloquial than 不禁. Implies the response was beyond your control.

examples.chinese: 聽到這消息,她不由得哭了起來。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào zhè xiāoxī, tā bùyóude kūle qǐlái.
examples.english: Hearing the news, she couldn't help but burst into tears.

english: by any means necessary; stop at nothing; unscrupulous
semanticNote: Strongly negative. Means using whatever methods are available regardless of ethics or legality — 'stop at nothing,' 'by fair means or foul.' Always about someone whose ambition or greed overrides moral constraints. 他為了升職不擇手段 = He'll do anything to get promoted. Not used admiringly; always a criticism. Compare to 不惜一切 (spare no effort — can be neutral/positive) which lacks the moral condemnation.

examples.chinese: 他為了達到目的，可以不擇手段。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèile dádào mùdì, kěyǐ bùzéshǒuduàn.
examples.english: To achieve his goals, he'll stop at nothing.

examples.chinese: 這家公司不擇手段地壓低成本，引發員工強烈不滿。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī bùzéshǒuduàn de yā dī chéngběn, yǐnfā yuángōng qiángliè bùmǎn.
examples.english: The company cut costs by any means necessary, sparking fierce employee discontent.

semanticNote: Two senses: (1) more than (a number) — 不止一次 (more than once), 不止三十歲 (more than thirty years old); (2) without stopping — 笑個不止 (laughing nonstop), 流血不止 (bleeding non-stop). Context disambiguates which sense applies.

examples.chinese: 我去過那裡不止一次。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qùguò nàlǐ bùzhǐ yí cì.
examples.english: I've been there more than once.

semanticNote: A public notice posted on a board or wall — bulletin-style announcement. 布告欄 = bulletin board. Old-school institutional communication; less common as digital messaging takes over, but still used in schools, offices, government buildings.

examples.chinese: 學校在布告欄貼了通知。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào zài bùgàolán tiēle tōngzhī.
examples.english: The school posted a notice on the bulletin board.

semanticNote: Spatial or strategic arrangement — chess game (棋局的布局), city layout (城市布局), business strategy (戰略布局). Both physical layouts and abstract positioning. Common in design, urban planning, and strategic discussions.

examples.chinese: 這家店的布局很合理。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de bùjú hěn hélǐ.
examples.english: This shop's layout is well-designed.

semanticNote: To arrange or set up — a room (布置房間 = decorate a room), a task (布置作業 = assign homework), a venue for an event. Common everyday word for organizing physical spaces or assigning tasks. Teachers 布置 homework; party planners 布置 venues.

examples.chinese: 老師布置了很多作業。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī bùzhìle hěn duō zuòyè.
examples.english: The teacher assigned a lot of homework.

semanticNote: Pace or pacing — physical (a soldier's step) and figurative (跟上時代的步伐 = keep pace with the times, 加快步伐 = quicken the pace). Often used metaphorically about progress, development, or social change. Slightly literary.

examples.chinese: 我們要跟上時代的步伐。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào gēnshàng shídài de bùfá.
examples.english: We need to keep pace with the times.

semanticNote: Strategic deployment — military (deploy troops), corporate (deploy resources), tech (deploy software/systems). Implies organized, planned arrangement of assets toward a goal. 戰略部署 = strategic deployment. Top-down, planning-vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 公司部署了新的市場策略。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī bùshǔle xīn de shìchǎng cèlüè.
examples.english: The company deployed a new market strategy.

semanticNote: A specific part or area, most often of a body or object. 身體部位 = body part, 受傷部位 = injured area. Medical, anatomical, technical contexts. More precise than 地方 (place, generic).

examples.chinese: 請告訴我哪個部位疼。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gàosù wǒ nǎ ge bùwèi téng.
examples.english: Please tell me which part hurts.

semanticNote: Practical talent and capability, especially for getting things done in work or leadership. 有才幹的人 (a competent person). Compare to 才能 (talent, broader/more artistic) and 能力 (ability, neutral). 才幹 specifically connotes practical executive ability.

examples.chinese: 他是個有才幹的領導。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge yǒu cáigàn de lǐngdǎo.
examples.english: He's a competent leader.

semanticNote: Wealth — money, property, but also abstract: 精神財富 (spiritual wealth), 知識是財富 (knowledge is wealth). More dignified and broad than 錢 (money, concrete). Common in finance, philosophy, and inspirational contexts.

examples.chinese: 健康才是真正的財富。
examples.pinyin: Jiànkāng cái shì zhēnzhèng de cáifù.
examples.english: Health is the true wealth.

semanticNote: Business/personal finance management. 財務部 (finance department), 財務報表 (financial statements), 財務狀況 (financial situation). Different from 財政 (public/government finance) — 財務 is private/corporate.

examples.chinese: 她在公司負責財務工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gōngsī fùzé cáiwù gōngzuò.
