semanticNote: Two main uses: (1) put/place something somewhere — 把書擱在桌上 (put the book on the table); (2) set aside / shelve — 擱在一邊 (set it aside), 擱置爭議 (shelve the dispute). The 'shelve' sense is very common in workplace/diplomatic contexts.

examples.chinese: 這個項目暫時擱一下。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiàngmù zànshí gē yíxià.
examples.english: Let's put this project on hold for now.

semanticNote: To cut — with a blade. 割肉 (cut meat), 割傷 (cut/laceration). Modern internet slang: 割韭菜 (literally 'cut the chives' = exploit gullible investors over and over).

examples.chinese: 他不小心割傷了手。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn gēshāngle shǒu.
examples.english: He accidentally cut his hand.

english: to extol; sing the praises of
semanticNote: To celebrate / sing praises of — usually grand subjects: motherland, heroes, love, virtues. 歌頌祖國 (extol the motherland). Reverent register; common in songs, poems, official speeches.

examples.chinese: 這首歌歌頌了母愛。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē gēsòngle mǔ'ài.
examples.english: This song sings the praises of motherly love.

semanticNote: Major political/social/technological revolution. 工業革命 (Industrial Revolution), 文化大革命 (Cultural Revolution), 革命家 (revolutionary). Heavy political weight in Chinese discourse.

examples.chinese: 互聯網引發了一場資訊革命。
examples.pinyin: Hùliánwǎng yǐnfāle yì chǎng zīxùn gémìng.
examples.english: The internet sparked an information revolution.

semanticNote: Two senses: (1) layout/structure — physical (房子的格局 = the layout of the house) or strategic (世界格局 = world structure/landscape); (2) someone's mental/strategic horizon — 沒有格局 (lacking vision/big-picture thinking). The vision sense has become trendy in business talk.

examples.chinese: 做事要有大格局。
examples.pinyin: Zuòshì yào yǒu dà géjú.
examples.english: You need to think with a big-picture mindset.

semanticNote: Format — documents, files, presentations. 文件格式 (file format), 格式化 (to format, both documents and disks). Tech and document-formatting vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 請按照標準格式寫報告。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng ànzhào biāozhǔn géshì xiě bàogào.
examples.english: Please write the report following the standard format.

semanticNote: Emotional/cultural/communication barrier between people or groups. 消除隔閡 (remove the barrier), 文化隔閡 (cultural divide). Often appears in discussions of relationships, diplomacy, family.

examples.chinese: 他們之間有些隔閡。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhī jiān yǒuxiē géhé.
examples.english: There's some estrangement between them.

semanticNote: To isolate / quarantine — public health (疫情期間隔離 = quarantine during epidemic), social (社會隔離 = social isolation). Massive presence in vocab during COVID. Also figurative.

examples.chinese: 確診患者必須隔離。
examples.pinyin: Quèzhěn huànzhě bìxū gélí.
examples.english: Confirmed cases must be quarantined.

semanticNote: Individual entity — person, organism. Pair with 群體 (group/collective). Used in sociology, biology, business (個體戶 = self-employed individual / sole proprietor in mainland legal terminology).

examples.chinese: 每個個體都是獨特的。
examples.pinyin: Měi ge gètǐ dōu shì dútè de.
examples.english: Every individual is unique.

semanticNote: Everyone freely expresses their own opinions in a discussion. 大家各抒己見 (everyone offered their views). Common in encouraging open discussion.

examples.chinese: 會上大家各抒己見。
examples.pinyin: Huì shàng dàjiā gèshūjǐjiàn.
examples.english: At the meeting, everyone shared their own views.

semanticNote: Deeply rooted — usually negative (prejudices, customs, problems). 根深蒂固的偏見 (deeply rooted prejudices). Implies hard to change, has been there a long time.

examples.chinese: 這種觀念根深蒂固。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng guānniàn gēnshēndìgù.
examples.english: This view is deeply ingrained.

semanticNote: Root cause / origin of a problem. 找出問題的根源 (find the root of the problem). Analytical word — distinguishes from 原因 (reason/cause, broader).

examples.chinese: 我們要從根源上解決問題。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào cóng gēnyuán shàng jiějué wèntí.
examples.english: We need to solve the problem at its root.

semanticNote: Right in front of / beside someone. 在我跟前 (in front of me / at my side). Slightly more colloquial than 面前. Casual register.

examples.chinese: 她坐在奶奶的跟前。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuò zài nǎinai de gēnqián.
examples.english: She sat right beside Grandma.

semanticNote: To follow — physically (walk behind) or figuratively (follow a leader, trend). 跟隨潮流 (follow the trend). Slightly more formal than 跟著.

examples.chinese: 小狗跟隨著主人。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu gēnsuízhe zhǔrén.
examples.english: The puppy follows its owner.

semanticNote: To track / shadow — covertly following someone (police tail, stalker, paparazzi) or tracking data/progress. 跟蹤調查 (follow-up investigation), 跟蹤報導 (follow-up coverage). Spy-thriller AND analytical contexts.

examples.chinese: 她覺得有人在跟蹤她。
examples.pinyin: Tā juéde yǒu rén zài gēnzōng tā.
examples.english: She felt someone was following her.

semanticNote: To update / renew — software (軟體更新 = software update), data, equipment, oneself. Modern essential vocabulary. Note tone: 更 here read gēng, not gèng.

examples.chinese: 請更新到最新版本。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gēngxīn dào zuì xīn bǎnběn.
examples.english: Please update to the latest version.

semanticNote: To formally correct an error in published or stated information. 更正啟事 (correction notice, in newspapers). Formal register. Compare to 改正 (correct, broader/everyday).

examples.chinese: 報紙更正了昨天的錯誤報導。
examples.pinyin: Bàozhǐ gēngzhèngle zuótiān de cuòwù bàodǎo.
examples.english: The newspaper corrected yesterday's erroneous report.

semanticNote: Two senses: (1) to plow farmland; (2) arable land as a noun (耕地面積 = arable land area). Agricultural vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 中國的耕地越來越少。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó de gēngdì yuèláiyuè shǎo.
examples.english: China's arable land is shrinking.

semanticNote: Handcrafted artisan goods — pottery, wood carving, embroidery, jade work. Common souvenir vocabulary in Chinese tourism.

examples.chinese: 我買了一些當地的工藝品。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎile yìxiē dāngdì de gōngyìpǐn.
examples.english: I bought some local handicrafts.

semanticNote: Mainland China's term for police bureau. 公安 alone = police (mainland). Taiwan uses 警察局 instead. Officially the institutional name in PRC.

examples.chinese: 他去公安局報案。
examples.pinyin: Tā qù gōng'ānjú bào'àn.
examples.english: He went to the public security bureau to file a report.

semanticNote: Fair/just — prices (價格公道 = reasonable price), treatment (公道一點 = be fair). Also noun: 討公道 (demand justice / get a fair shake). Old-school justice-flavored word.

examples.chinese: 這家店價錢很公道。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn jiàqián hěn gōngdao.
examples.english: This shop has very fair prices.

semanticNote: Official public announcement — government notices, corporate disclosures, building bulletin board notices. More official than 通知 (notification).

examples.chinese: 請看公告欄上的最新公告。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng kàn gōnggàolán shàng de zuìxīn gōnggào.
examples.english: Please check the latest announcement on the notice board.

semanticNote: Public relations. 公關危機 (PR crisis), 公關人員 (PR personnel). Modern business vocabulary. Sometimes ironic — 'this is PR' = damage control / spin.

examples.chinese: 她在公關部門工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gōngguān bùmén gōngzuò.
examples.english: She works in the PR department.

semanticNote: Citizen of a country — legal/political concept. 公民權利 (civil rights), 公民責任 (civic responsibility). More formal than 國民 (national).

examples.chinese: 每個公民都有投票權。
examples.pinyin: Měi ge gōngmín dōu yǒu tóupiào quán.
examples.english: Every citizen has the right to vote.

semanticNote: To do something openly without shame — usually negative actions done in defiance. 公然違法 (openly break the law), 公然挑釁 (brazenly provoke). Critical tone — implies the person didn't even bother to hide it.

examples.chinese: 他公然違反規定。
examples.pinyin: Tā gōngrán wéifǎn guīdìng.
examples.english: He openly violated the rules.

semanticNote: Recognized by everyone. 公認的事實 (a generally acknowledged fact), 公認的權威 (widely recognized authority). Implies broad consensus.

examples.chinese: 她是公認的最佳選手。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gōngrèn de zuì jiā xuǎnshǒu.
examples.english: She's generally recognized as the best player.

semanticNote: Mathematical/scientific formula. 數學公式 (math formula), 化學公式 (chemical formula). Also figurative: 成功的公式 (formula for success). Academic and analytical.

examples.chinese: 請記住這個數學公式。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jìzhù zhè ge shùxué gōngshì.
examples.english: Please memorize this math formula.

semanticNote: Official duties — government, civil service. 公務員 (civil servant — coveted job in China/Taiwan), 出公差 (go on official business trip). Government-employee vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 他是一名公務員。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yì míng gōngwùyuán.
examples.english: He's a civil servant.

semanticNote: Just/fair/impartial — judges, decisions, treatment. 公正的判決 (a fair verdict). Slightly more formal than 公道 (fair, casual). Heavy moral weight.

examples.chinese: 法官的判決必須公正。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān de pànjué bìxū gōngzhèng.
examples.english: A judge's verdict must be impartial.

semanticNote: Legal notarization — having a document officially certified by a notary. 公證處 (notary office), 公證書 (notarized document). Legal vocabulary, important for international document recognition.

examples.chinese: 這份文件需要公證。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn wénjiàn xūyào gōngzhèng.
examples.english: This document needs to be notarized.

semanticNote: Credit for achievements. 立下大功勞 (made a great contribution), 沒有功勞也有苦勞 (even if no merit, at least put in the hard work — common Chinese saying). Common in workplace and team contexts.

examples.chinese: 這次成功是大家的功勞。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì chénggōng shì dàjiā de gōngláo.
examples.english: This success is everyone's contribution.

semanticNote: Tangible effects of medicine, products, methods. 藥的功效 (efficacy of the drug), 顯著的功效 (notable effect). Pharmaceutical and beauty product vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 這種藥的功效很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào de gōngxiào hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This medicine is very effective.

semanticNote: To attack — military, verbal, in sports/games. 言語攻擊 (verbal attack), 網路攻擊 (cyberattack). Also figurative: 人身攻擊 = personal attack (in arguments). Common across many contexts.

examples.chinese: 他在會議上攻擊了我的觀點。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài huìyì shàng gōngjīle wǒ de guāndiǎn.
examples.english: He attacked my viewpoint at the meeting.

semanticNote: To capture militarily, or figuratively overcome a difficulty. 攻克難關 (overcome a tough challenge), 攻克技術難題 (crack a technical problem). Achievement-oriented word.

examples.chinese: 科學家終於攻克了這個難題。
examples.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā zhōngyú gōngkèle zhè ge nántí.
examples.english: Scientists finally cracked this problem.

semanticNote: Supply can't keep up with demand. Common in business/economics. Pair with 供過於求 (supply exceeds demand). News and market analysis vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 這款手機供不應求。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn shǒujī gōngbúyìngqiú.
examples.english: Demand for this phone exceeds supply.

semanticNote: To provide supply — goods, resources, services. 供給商 (supplier). Economics vocabulary; pair with 需求 (demand). Note tone: 給 here read jǐ.

examples.chinese: 這個地區的水電供給很穩定。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge dìqū de shuǐdiàn gōngjǐ hěn wěndìng.
examples.english: This region has stable water and electricity supply.

semanticNote: Palace — for emperors and kings. 故宮 = the Forbidden City (the most famous palace in China). Tourist and historical vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 這座宮殿建於唐朝。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò gōngdiàn jiàn yú Tángcháo.
examples.english: This palace was built in the Tang Dynasty.

semanticNote: Respectful — in attitude and behavior, especially toward elders/superiors. 恭敬地行禮 (bow respectfully). More formal/visible than 尊敬 (respect, internal feeling).

examples.chinese: 他恭敬地向老師鞠躬。
examples.pinyin: Tā gōngjìng de xiàng lǎoshī jūgōng.
examples.english: He bowed respectfully to the teacher.

semanticNote: To strengthen/consolidate — knowledge (鞏固知識 = consolidate what you've learned), positions, relationships, achievements. Common in education and political contexts.

examples.chinese: 複習能鞏固所學的知識。
examples.pinyin: Fùxí néng gǒnggù suǒ xué de zhīshì.
examples.english: Review consolidates what you've learned.

semanticNote: Republic (form of government). 中華人民共和國 (People's Republic of China), 中華民國 (Republic of China — Taiwan). Heavy political/historical vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 中華人民共和國成立於1949年。
examples.pinyin: Zhōnghuá Rénmín Gònghéguó chénglì yú yī jiǔ sì jiǔ nián.
examples.english: The People's Republic of China was founded in 1949.

semanticNote: To total / sum up. 共計一百萬 (totaling a million). Used in financial summaries, reports, calculations.

examples.chinese: 這次活動共計花費十萬元。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì huódòng gòngjì huāfèi shí wàn yuán.
examples.english: This event cost a total of 100,000 yuan.

semanticNote: Two senses: (1) physical resonance; (2) figurative emotional resonance — 引起共鳴 (resonate, strike a chord). The figurative sense dominates everyday speech — about songs, films, books, ideas that connect with people.

examples.chinese: 這首歌引起了我的共鳴。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē yǐnqǐle wǒ de gòngmíng.
examples.english: This song really resonated with me.

semanticNote: To collude — illegal/conspiratorial cooperation. 內外勾結 (inside-outside collusion). Always negative — implies criminal or unethical alliance.

examples.chinese: 他被指控與不法分子勾結。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi zhǐkòng yǔ bùfǎ fènzǐ gōujié.
examples.english: He was accused of colluding with criminals.

semanticNote: A physical hook — for hanging things, fishing. 衣鉤 (clothes hook), 釣魚鉤 (fishhook). Also figurative in some compounds.

examples.chinese: 請把外套掛在鉤子上。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ wàitào guà zài gōuzi shàng.
examples.english: Please hang your coat on the hook.

semanticNote: To brainstorm/outline — for creative works, designs, articles. 構思劇情 (plot a story), 巧妙的構思 (clever conception). Creative process vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 作家正在構思新小說。
examples.pinyin: Zuòjiā zhèngzài gòusī xīn xiǎoshuō.
examples.english: The writer is conceiving a new novel.

semanticNote: The ache of being alone or feeling alone even among people. More literary and existential than 寂寞 (loneliness as boredom or emptiness from lack of company). 孤獨 can be a chosen state (the solitude of a hermit or artist) but still carries a note of isolation. 我感到孤獨 = I feel lonely. 孤獨感 = sense of isolation. Taiwan usage: both words are common, but 孤獨 appears more in written, literary contexts while 寂寞 is more casual and conversational. 孤 alone means orphaned/solitary; 獨 means alone/only.

examples.chinese: 搬到新城市後，她感到非常孤獨。
examples.pinyin: Bān dào xīn chéngshì hòu, tā gǎndào fēicháng gūdú.
examples.english: After moving to a new city, she felt deeply lonely.

examples.chinese: 即使在人群中，他也常常感到孤獨。
examples.pinyin: Jíshǐ zài rénqún zhōng, tā yě chángcháng gǎndào gūdú.
examples.english: Even in a crowd, he often feels alone.

semanticNote: Isolated — physically (孤立的島嶼 = an isolated island) or socially/diplomatically (在國際上被孤立 = isolated internationally). Often negative — implies cut off and alone.

examples.chinese: 他在公司被同事孤立了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gōngsī bèi tóngshì gūlì le.
examples.english: He's been isolated by his coworkers.

semanticNote: 'For now / tentatively' — a temporary arrangement or provisional acceptance. 姑且這樣做 (let's do it this way for now), 姑且不論 (setting aside for now). Slightly literary register.

examples.chinese: 我們姑且試一試。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gūqiě shì yi shì.
examples.english: Let's give it a try for now.

semanticNote: To disappoint someone who had high hopes/trust in you. 辜負期望 (let down expectations), 不辜負父母 (don't let your parents down). Heavy emotional weight — implies failing someone's faith in you.

examples.chinese: 我不會辜負你的信任。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú huì gūfù nǐ de xìnrèn.
examples.english: I won't betray your trust.

semanticNote: Antique. 古董店 (antique shop), 收藏古董 (collect antiques). Also affectionate/joking term for someone old-fashioned: 老古董 (an old antique = a fuddy-duddy).

examples.chinese: 奶奶有許多珍貴的古董。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai yǒu xǔduō zhēnguì de gǔdǒng.
examples.english: Grandma has many valuable antiques.

semanticNote: Strange and unusual — usually about people's behavior or thinking. 古怪的人 (an eccentric person), 脾氣古怪 (a quirky temper). Less harsh than 奇怪 (strange, neutral) — 古怪 has a flavor of 'odd in an interesting way.'

examples.chinese: 那位老人有點古怪。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi lǎorén yǒudiǎn gǔguài.
examples.english: That old man is a bit eccentric.

semanticNote: Shareholder — owns shares in a company. 股東大會 (shareholders' meeting), 主要股東 (major shareholder). Standard business/finance vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 他是公司的大股東。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gōngsī de dà gǔdōng.
examples.english: He's a major shareholder in the company.

semanticNote: Stock/equity in a company. 股份有限公司 (limited liability company), 持有股份 (hold shares). Business and investment vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 她持有公司10%的股份。
examples.pinyin: Tā chíyǒu gōngsī bǎi fēn zhī shí de gǔfèn.
examples.english: She holds 10% of the company's shares.

semanticNote: Backbone / core member of an organization or team. 骨幹力量 (backbone force), 公司的骨幹 (company's core people). Implies essential, indispensable role.

examples.chinese: 她是團隊的骨幹。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì tuánduì de gǔgàn.
examples.english: She's the backbone of the team.

semanticNote: To stir up / agitate / urge people to act. Often negative — implies manipulating people into action. 鼓動造反 (incite rebellion). Compare to 鼓勵 (encourage, positive). 鼓動 has a manipulative tinge.

examples.chinese: 他鼓動工人罷工。
examples.pinyin: Tā gǔdòng gōngrén bàgōng.
examples.english: He incited the workers to strike.

semanticNote: 'Admittedly... but...' — concessive conjunction. 努力固然重要,但方法也很重要 (Effort is admittedly important, but method matters too). Common in argumentative writing.

examples.chinese: 金錢固然重要,但健康更重要。
examples.pinyin: Jīnqián gùrán zhòngyào, dàn jiànkāng gèng zhòngyào.
examples.english: Money is admittedly important, but health matters more.

semanticNote: Solid state. Pair with 液體 (liquid) and 氣體 (gas). Science vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 水冷凍後變成固體。
examples.pinyin: Shuǐ lěngdòng hòu biànchéng gùtǐ.
examples.english: Water becomes a solid when frozen.

semanticNote: Intrinsic/inherent — built-in, native to something. 固有的特質 (inherent qualities), 固有觀念 (entrenched preconceptions). Analytical word.

examples.chinese: 每個民族都有固有的文化。
examples.pinyin: Měi ge mínzú dōu yǒu gùyǒu de wénhuà.
examples.english: Every nation has its inherent culture.

semanticNote: Stubborn — won't change one's mind even when wrong. 固執己見 (stubbornly hold to one's own view). Mostly negative; can occasionally be praise (固執地追求夢想 = stubbornly pursue one's dream).

examples.chinese: 他很固執,不聽別人勸告。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn gùzhí, bù tīng biérén quàngào.
examples.english: He's stubborn and won't listen to others' advice.

semanticNote: Hometown / homeland — emotionally weighted word. 思念故鄉 (long for one's hometown). More poetic than 老家 (hometown, casual). Common in literature and songs about homesickness.

examples.chinese: 離開故鄉多年,我很想念。
examples.pinyin: Líkāi gùxiāng duō nián, wǒ hěn xiǎngniàn.
examples.english: After years away from home, I miss it deeply.

semanticNote: Mechanical/technical malfunction. 機器故障 (machine breakdown), 電腦故障 (computer malfunction), 故障率 (failure rate). Tech and engineering vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 電梯出現故障了。
examples.pinyin: Diàntī chūxiàn gùzhàng le.
examples.english: The elevator has malfunctioned.

semanticNote: Concerns/worries that hold you back from acting. 打消顧慮 (dispel concerns). Common in workplace and personal decision-making contexts.

examples.chinese: 她對這個計劃還有些顧慮。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhè ge jìhuà hái yǒuxiē gùlǜ.
examples.english: She still has some concerns about this plan.

semanticNote: Advisor/consultant. 法律顧問 (legal counsel), 顧問公司 (consulting firm). Modern business vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 他是公司的法律顧問。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gōngsī de fǎlǜ gùwèn.
examples.english: He's the company's legal advisor.

semanticNote: To hire — formal employment relationship. 僱傭關係 (employment relationship), 僱傭兵 (mercenary). Slightly more formal than 僱 (hire) alone. Legal/business vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 公司僱傭了一百名員工。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī gùyōngle yìbǎi míng yuángōng.
examples.english: The company employs a hundred staff.

semanticNote: Walking stick / crutch — for elderly or injured. Also figurative: emotional crutch. Practical word in healthcare and elder-care contexts.

examples.chinese: 爺爺需要拐杖才能走路。
examples.pinyin: Yéye xūyào guǎizhàng cáinéng zǒulù.
examples.english: Grandpa needs a walking stick to walk.

semanticNote: Warm caring concern — for elders, sick, vulnerable. More formal/tender than 關心 (care about, everyday). 關懷弱勢 (care for the disadvantaged). Has a slight institutional flavor too — used in NGO and policy contexts.

examples.chinese: 我們應該關懷孤寡老人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi guānhuái gūguǎ lǎorén.
examples.english: We should care for elderly people who are alone.

english: to look after; keep an eye on; (polite) regard
semanticNote: Two senses: (1) take care of/keep an eye on — 關照孩子 (look after kids), 請多關照 (please take good care of me — common polite phrase when meeting new colleagues); (2) inform someone of something. The 'please look after me' use is a bow to East Asian social courtesy.

examples.chinese: 請多多關照。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng duōduō guānzhào.
examples.english: Please look out for me. (polite formula)

semanticNote: Sightseeing / tourism. 觀光客 (tourist), 觀光景點 (tourist spot), 觀光業 (tourism industry). Travel vocabulary; 觀光 specifically implies seeing the sights, not just travel.

examples.chinese: 我們去日本觀光。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen qù Rìběn guānguāng.
examples.english: We're going sightseeing in Japan.

semanticNote: Official — coming from government or organization itself. 官方聲明 (official statement), 官方網站 (official website). Modern internet slang: 官方 has come to mean 'authoritative' / 'authentic' in fan culture (the 'official' canon of a story).

examples.chinese: 請參考官方公告。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng cānkǎo guānfāng gōnggào.
examples.english: Please refer to the official announcement.

semanticNote: Legal/administrative jurisdiction. 管轄範圍 (jurisdiction / scope of authority), 不在我們管轄之內 (outside our jurisdiction). Government and legal vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 這個地區歸這個法院管轄。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge dìqū guī zhè ge fǎyuàn guǎnxiá.
examples.english: This area falls under this court's jurisdiction.

semanticNote: To carry through fully — policies, decisions, plans. 貫徹執行 (implement thoroughly), 貫徹始終 (carry through to the end). Government/management vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 我們要貫徹這項政策。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào guànchè zhè xiàng zhèngcè.
examples.english: We must thoroughly implement this policy.

semanticNote: Established custom or convention — informal but commonly followed practice. 按照慣例 (as is customary), 國際慣例 (international convention/norm). Different from 習慣 (habit, individual) — 慣例 is collective practice.

examples.chinese: 按照慣例,新年要拜訪長輩。
examples.pinyin: Ànzhào guànlì, xīnnián yào bàifǎng zhǎngbèi.
examples.english: As is customary, we visit elders during New Year.

semanticNote: Agricultural irrigation. 灌溉系統 (irrigation system), 灌溉農田 (irrigate fields). Agricultural and infrastructure vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 農民用河水灌溉農田。
examples.pinyin: Nóngmín yòng héshuǐ guàngài nóngtián.
examples.english: Farmers use river water to irrigate fields.

semanticNote: Container — can, jar. Also measure word for canned things: 一罐可樂 (a can of cola), 一罐果醬 (a jar of jam). Practical everyday word.

examples.chinese: 我買了三罐啤酒。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎile sān guàn píjiǔ.
examples.english: I bought three cans of beer.

semanticNote: Two senses: (1) literal luster/radiance; (2) figurative honor/glory — 為國爭光彩 (bring honor to the country). 不光彩 = dishonorable/shameful. Often used as a moral/social judgment word.

examples.chinese: 作弊不是一件光彩的事。
examples.pinyin: Zuòbì bú shì yí jiàn guāngcǎi de shì.
examples.english: Cheating is not an honorable thing.

semanticNote: Brilliant radiance — physical (光輝燦爛 = brilliantly radiant) or figurative (光輝的歷史 = glorious history, 光輝形象 = glorious image). Reverent/elevated register.

examples.chinese: 這是民族光輝的歷史。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì mínzú guānghuī de lìshǐ.
examples.english: This is the glorious history of the nation.

semanticNote: Rays of light — sun, stars, fire. Often figurative: 散發光芒 (radiate brilliance). Poetic register.

examples.chinese: 陽光的光芒非常耀眼。
examples.pinyin: Yángguāng de guāngmáng fēicháng yàoyǎn.
examples.english: The rays of the sun are dazzling.

semanticNote: Glory/honor — usually for accomplishments, sacrifices, sports victories. 光榮的傳統 (glorious tradition). 為國爭光榮 = bring glory to the country. Grand register.

examples.chinese: 當奧運選手是無上光榮。
examples.pinyin: Dāng Àoyùn xuǎnshǒu shì wúshàng guāngróng.
examples.english: Being an Olympic athlete is the highest honor.

semanticNote: Vast and open — physical (廣闊的草原 = vast grasslands) or figurative (廣闊的視野 = broad horizon, 廣闊的前景 = broad prospects). Implies expansiveness.

examples.chinese: 這個年輕人有廣闊的前景。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge niánqīngrén yǒu guǎngkuò de qiánjǐng.
examples.english: This young person has broad prospects.

semanticNote: 'When you trace it to the root' — used to emphasize the fundamental cause/conclusion. 歸根到底還是錢的問題 (in the end, it's a money issue). Common in summarizing arguments.

examples.chinese: 歸根到底,還是健康最重要。
examples.pinyin: Guīgēndàodǐ, háishì jiànkāng zuì zhòngyào.
examples.english: In the final analysis, health matters most.

semanticNote: To return borrowed items. 歸還圖書 (return library books). More formal than 還 alone. Library, lending, and legal contexts.

examples.chinese: 請按時歸還圖書。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng ànshí guīhuán túshū.
examples.english: Please return books on time.

semanticNote: Standard/norm — both noun (a standard) and verb (to standardize, regulate). 行為規範 (code of conduct), 規範市場 (regulate the market). Common in management, education, and policy.

examples.chinese: 我們要規範員工的行為。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào guīfàn yuángōng de xíngwéi.
examples.english: We need to standardize employee conduct.

semanticNote: Product specs — size, quality standards. 不同規格 (different specifications). Manufacturing, retail, technical vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 請告訴我這個產品的規格。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gàosù wǒ zhè ge chǎnpǐn de guīgé.
examples.english: Please tell me this product's specifications.

semanticNote: Strategic long-term planning — city planning, life planning, career planning. 城市規劃 (urban planning), 職業規劃 (career planning). More substantial than 計劃 (plan) — implies bigger-picture, multi-year vision.

examples.chinese: 她對未來有清晰的規劃。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì wèilái yǒu qīngxī de guīhuà.
examples.english: She has a clear plan for the future.

semanticNote: Rules and regulations — institutional. 規章制度 (rules and regulations). Common in workplace and institutional contexts.

examples.chinese: 請遵守公司規章。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zūnshǒu gōngsī guīzhāng.
examples.english: Please follow company rules.

semanticNote: Three senses: (1) train track (火車軌道); (2) celestial orbit (衛星軌道 = satellite orbit); (3) figurative right course/path — 步入正軌 (get on the right track). Versatile word.

examples.chinese: 工作終於步入了正軌。
examples.pinyin: Gōngzuò zhōngyú bùrùle zhèngguǐ.
examples.english: Work has finally gotten on the right track.

semanticNote: Aristocracy — historical (European/Chinese imperial), cultural, or modern figurative ('elite class'). 貴族學校 = elite school. Period drama and historical vocabulary, also marketing (suggesting luxury).

examples.chinese: 這所貴族學校學費非常高。
examples.pinyin: Zhè suǒ guìzú xuéxiào xuéfèi fēicháng gāo.
examples.english: This elite school's tuition is extremely high.

semanticNote: To kneel — religious worship, traditional respect, begging, surrender. 跪下 (kneel down). Modern internet slang: 我跪了 = 'I'm bowing down to you' (= 'I'm impressed, you win'). Casual exclamation of being amazed/defeated.

examples.chinese: 信徒跪在佛像前。
examples.pinyin: Xìntú guì zài fóxiàng qián.
examples.english: The believer knelt before the Buddha statue.

semanticNote: Stick or club — usually as weapon. 棍棒教育 (corporal punishment / 'beating-stick' style of parenting). Often appears in discussions of discipline and parenting.

examples.chinese: 棍棒底下出孝子是過時的觀念。
examples.pinyin: Gùnbàng dǐxia chū xiàozǐ shì guòshí de guānniàn.
examples.english: 'Spare the rod, spoil the child' is an outdated idea.

semanticNote: National defense. 國防部 (Ministry of Defense), 國防預算 (defense budget). Government and military vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 國家增加了國防預算。
examples.pinyin: Guójiā zēngjiāle guófáng yùsuàn.
examples.english: The country increased its defense budget.

semanticNote: Two referents depending on context: (1) State Council — the chief administrative body of the PRC; (2) State Department — the US government department for foreign affairs. Government/news vocabulary.

examples.chinese: 國務院發布了新的政策。
examples.pinyin: Guówùyuàn fābùle xīn de zhèngcè.
examples.english: The State Council issued a new policy.

semanticNote: Acting decisively without hesitation. 果斷 describes a person who makes up their mind quickly and firmly — 行動果斷 (act decisively), 果斷的決定 (a decisive decision). Positive quality; contrasts with 猶豫 (hesitant) and 優柔寡斷 (wishy-washy). The 果 here means 'resolute result' (same as 結果 fruit/result) — your action bears fruit because you commit.

examples.chinese: 面對危機，領導者必須果斷行動。
examples.pinyin: Miànduì wéijī, lǐngdǎozhě bìxū guǒduàn xíngdòng.
examples.english: Facing a crisis, leaders must act decisively.

examples.chinese: 她果斷地拒絕了那份不合理的合約。
examples.pinyin: Tā guǒduàn de jùjuéle nà fèn bùhélǐ de héyuē.
examples.english: She decisively turned down that unreasonable contract.

semanticNote: Doing or having too much of something — 過度疲勞 (over-fatigued), 過度消費 (excessive consumption), 過度緊張 (over-anxious). Functions as both adjective and adverb. Homophone alert: 過渡 (5729) means 'transition' — same pinyin guòdù, completely different meaning. 過度 = excess; 過渡 = transition/crossing over. Context almost always disambiguates but tone-deafness between the two is a common learner error.

examples.chinese: 過度使用手機會影響睡眠品質。
examples.pinyin: Guòdù shǐyòng shǒujī huì yǐngxiǎng shuìmián pǐnzhì.
examples.english: Excessive phone use affects sleep quality.

examples.chinese: 醫生說他過度勞累，需要好好休息。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō tā guòdù láolèi, xūyào hǎohǎo xiūxi.
examples.english: The doctor said he was over-fatigued and needed proper rest.

semanticNote: Moving from one state or system to another — 過渡期 (transition period), 過渡政府 (interim government), 過渡階段 (transitional phase). The literal meaning is crossing a river by ferry — a passage between two banks. Now almost exclusively metaphorical in modern use. Common in political and economic contexts. Homophone: 過度 (excessive). 過渡 = crossing a gap; 過度 = going too far.

examples.chinese: 這是一個過渡時期，很多政策還在調整中。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge guòdù shíqī, hěn duō zhèngcè hái zài tiáozhěng zhōng.
examples.english: This is a transitional period — many policies are still being adjusted.

examples.chinese: 公司正在從傳統業務過渡到線上模式。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī zhèngzài cóng chuántǒng yèwù guòdù dào xiàn shàng móshì.
examples.english: The company is transitioning from traditional business to an online model.

semanticNote: A set-phrase humble response to a compliment — 'you're too kind,' 'I don't deserve such praise.' 您過獎了 is the standard polite deflection when someone praises you. It's a performative modesty move, not a genuine denial. In Taiwan this kind of gracious self-deprecation is expected; accepting a compliment directly would seem arrogant. Purely formulaic — you'd never use 過獎 to genuinely accuse someone of flattery.

examples.chinese: 「你的中文說得真好！」「過獎了，還差得遠呢。」
examples.pinyin: 「Nǐ de Zhōngwén shuō de zhēn hǎo!」「Guòjiǎng le, hái chà de yuǎn ne.」
examples.english: "Your Mandarin is excellent!" "You flatter me — I still have a long way to go."

examples.chinese: 您過獎了，這只是我應盡的本分。
examples.pinyin: Nín guòjiǎng le, zhè zhǐshì wǒ yīng jìn de běnfèn.
examples.english: You're too kind — this is just my duty.

semanticNote: Filtering out unwanted elements — physically (過濾水 = filter water, 過濾器 = filter) or metaphorically (過濾信息 = filter information, 過濾掉不良內容 = screen out harmful content). Very common in tech contexts: spam filters, content moderation, search algorithms all 過濾. The metaphorical use is now just as common as the physical.

examples.chinese: 這款淨水器可以過濾掉水中的雜質。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn jìnshuǐqì kěyǐ guòlǜ diào shuǐ zhōng de zázhì.
examples.english: This water purifier can filter out impurities in the water.

examples.chinese: 平台會自動過濾不當言論。
examples.pinyin: Píngtái huì zìdòng guòlǜ bùdàng yánlùn.
examples.english: The platform automatically filters out inappropriate content.

semanticNote: An error or negligence — especially in legal/formal contexts. 過失殺人 = manslaughter (negligent homicide, as opposed to intentional murder 故意殺人). Different from 錯誤 (mistake — general, neutral) in that 過失 implies a lapse of duty or care that caused harm. Formal register; you wouldn't say 今天我犯了個過失 about forgetting your umbrella — save it for genuine negligence.

examples.chinese: 他因工作上的過失被公司開除。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīn gōngzuò shàng de guòshī bèi gōngsī kāichú.
examples.english: He was fired for negligence on the job.

examples.chinese: 法庭判定這是一起過失傷害案。
examples.pinyin: Fǎtíng pàndìng zhè shì yī qǐ guòshī shānghài àn.
examples.english: The court ruled this was a case of negligent injury.

english: to ask about; get involved in; take an interest in
semanticNote: To take the trouble to inquire about or involve oneself in something. Often used in negative constructions: 沒人過問 (nobody bothered to ask / nobody cared), 不過問 (not get involved in). Can be neutral (showing concern) or imply unwanted interference depending on context. 你別過問我的事 = mind your own business. 沒有人過問災民的情況 = no one inquired about the disaster victims' condition (neglect).

examples.chinese: 這件事沒有人過問，就這樣不了了之。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì méiyǒu rén guòwèn, jiù zhèyàng bùliǎo liǎozhī.
examples.english: Nobody followed up on this matter and it just fizzled out.

examples.chinese: 父母應該過問孩子在學校的情況。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ yīnggāi guòwèn háizi zài xuéxiào de qíngkuàng.
examples.english: Parents should take an interest in how their children are doing at school.

english: satisfying; to get one's fill; do to one's heart's content
semanticNote: The satisfying feeling of fully indulging in something you enjoy — 'hitting the spot,' 'getting your fix.' 癮 literally means addiction/craving, so 過癮 = satisfying the craving. 看球賽看得很過癮 (watched the game to my heart's content), 這頓飯吃得真過癮 (that meal really hit the spot). Always positive and colloquial. Common in spoken Taiwan Mandarin.

examples.chinese: 今天的演唱會真的很過癮！
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de yǎnchànghuì zhēnde hěn guòyǐn!
examples.english: Tonight's concert was incredibly satisfying!

examples.chinese: 打了三小時的籃球，終於過癮了。
examples.pinyin: Dǎle sān xiǎoshí de lánqiú, zhōngyú guòyǐn le.
examples.english: Three hours of basketball — finally got my fill.

semanticNote: A formal/written-register adverb meaning 'excessively' or 'too.' 過于謹慎 (overly cautious), 過于樂觀 (excessively optimistic). More literary than 太 (too) — you'd use 過于 in essays and formal writing, 太 in casual conversation. Never used positively; always implies the quality described has gone beyond what's appropriate. Taiwan usage: you'll see it in editorial pieces and formal reports.

examples.chinese: 他做事過于謹慎，常常錯失機會。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuòshì guòyú jǐnshèn, chángcháng cuòshī jīhuì.
examples.english: He's overly cautious in everything he does and often misses opportunities.

examples.chinese: 這個要求過于苛刻，很難達到。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yāoqiú guòyú kēkè, hěn nán dádào.
examples.english: This requirement is excessively harsh and hard to meet.

semanticNote: Two distinct uses: (1) 嗨 hāi = casual 'hi' or 'hey,' borrowed from English — common in youth speech and online chats; (2) 嗨 hāi = a sigh expressing regret or disappointment, similar to 唉. The greeting use is dominant in Taiwan modern speech. Also used in the phrase 嗨起來 (get hyped up / party hard). Context makes the meaning clear.

examples.chinese: 嗨！好久不見，最近還好嗎？
examples.pinyin: Hāi! Hǎojiǔ bújiàn, zuìjìn hái hǎo ma?
examples.english: Hey! Long time no see — how have you been?

examples.chinese: 嗨，早知道就不去了。
examples.pinyin: Hāi, zǎo zhīdào jiù bú qù le.
examples.english: Sigh — if I'd known, I wouldn't have gone.

semanticNote: The technical term for elevation measured from sea level — 海拔一千公尺 (1,000 meters above sea level). Used in geography, weather forecasts, and travel writing. 海 = sea, 拔 = to pull up — the image is of something pulled up from the sea surface. Common in Taiwan travel content about mountain hiking, since Taiwan has numerous high-altitude peaks including 玉山 (Jade Mountain, ~3,952m).

examples.chinese: 玉山海拔將近四千公尺，是台灣最高的山。
examples.pinyin: Yùshān hǎibá jiāng jìn sìqiān gōngchǐ, shì Táiwān zuìgāo de shān.
examples.english: Jade Mountain is nearly 4,000 meters above sea level — Taiwan's highest peak.

examples.chinese: 高海拔地區空氣稀薄，容易高山症。
examples.pinyin: Gāo hǎibá dìqū kōngqì xībó, róngyì gāoshānzhèng.
examples.english: High-altitude areas have thin air and altitude sickness is common.

semanticNote: The area along the sea coast — more literary and formal than 海邊 (seaside — everyday spoken word). 海濱城市 (coastal city), 海濱公園 (beachfront park), 海濱度假村 (seaside resort). You'd use 海濱 in written descriptions and travel writing; in casual speech you'd say 海邊. Taiwan's east coast (東海岸) and Kenting (墾丁) are classic 海濱 destinations.

examples.chinese: 他們在海濱小屋住了一個星期。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài hǎibīn xiǎowū zhùle yí ge xīngqī.
examples.english: They spent a week in a seaside cottage.

examples.chinese: 夕陽下的海濱景色美得令人窒息。
examples.pinyin: Xīyáng xià de hǎibīn jǐngsè měi de lìng rén zhìxī.
examples.english: The seaside scenery at sunset is breathtakingly beautiful.

semanticNote: Something that's not clear or is deliberately evasive — 含糊其辭 (speak ambiguously, hedge). Also means careless or sloppy: 做事不能含糊 (you can't be sloppy in what you do). The careless use is common in Taiwan — 這件事不能含糊帶過 (you can't gloss over this carelessly). Different from 模糊 (blurry/fuzzy — more about visual or conceptual fuzziness) — 含糊 implies intentional or behavioral vagueness.

examples.chinese: 他的回答很含糊，根本不知道他的立場。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huídá hěn hánhu, gēnběn bù zhīdào tā de lìchǎng.
examples.english: His answer was so vague you couldn't tell where he stood.

examples.chinese: 這種事不能含糊，一定要說清楚。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng shì bù néng hánhu, yídìng yào shuō qīngchǔ.
examples.english: You can't be vague about something like this — it needs to be said clearly.

semanticNote: The meaning contained within — especially implicit or layered meaning. 這首詩含義深遠 (this poem has profound meaning). Different from 意思 (meaning — straightforward denotation) and 意義 (significance/meaning — often about importance or purpose). 含義 specifically implies something beneath the surface that needs to be drawn out. Common in literary analysis and philosophical discussion.

examples.chinese: 這幅畫的含義非常深刻，值得細細品味。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fú huà de hányì fēicháng shēnkè, zhídé xìxì pǐnwèi.
examples.english: The meaning embedded in this painting is profound — worth savoring carefully.

examples.chinese: 「平安」這個詞在中文裡含義豐富。
examples.pinyin: 「Píng'ān」 zhège cí zài Zhōngwén lǐ hányì fēngfù.
examples.english: The word 'peace and safety' carries rich connotations in Chinese.

semanticNote: The ritual exchange of greetings and pleasantries upon meeting — 'how are you,' 'nice weather,' 'how's the family.' 寒 (cold) and 暄 (warm) together suggest the seasonal small talk of asking about cold and warmth. Always slightly formulaic; it's the social lubricant of Mandarin conversation. 寒暄幾句 (exchange a few pleasantries). Common at the start of formal meetings or when greeting someone you haven't seen in a while.

examples.chinese: 兩人見面後先寒暄了幾句，才進入正題。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng rén jiànmiàn hòu xiān hánxuānle jǐ jù, cái jìnrù zhèngtí.
examples.english: The two exchanged a few pleasantries before getting down to business.

examples.chinese: 在台灣，見面時的寒暄是很重要的禮節。
examples.pinyin: Zài Táiwān, jiànmiàn shí de hánxuān shì hěn zhòngyào de lǐjié.
examples.english: In Taiwan, exchanging pleasantries when meeting is an important social courtesy.

semanticNote: Something rarely encountered. 罕見疾病 (rare disease), 罕見現象 (rare phenomenon), 百年罕見 (rare once in a century). More formal and emphatic than 少見 (seldom seen) or 稀有 (scarce/rare). Used in both positive and negative contexts — a 罕見的奇才 (a rare genius) vs 罕見的災難 (a rare disaster). Medical context: 罕見疾病 is the standard term for rare/orphan diseases.

examples.chinese: 台灣的雪景非常罕見，每次下雪都引起轟動。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān de xuějǐng fēicháng hǎnjiàn, měi cì xià xuě dōu yǐnqǐ hōngdòng.
examples.english: Snow scenery in Taiwan is very rare — every snowfall causes a sensation.

examples.chinese: 這是一種罕見的遺傳疾病，目前尚無特效藥。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī zhǒng hǎnjiàn de yíchuán jíbìng, mùqián shàng wú tèxiàoyào.
examples.english: This is a rare genetic disease with no effective treatment yet.

semanticNote: To actively defend or protect something under threat — 捍衛國家主權 (defend national sovereignty), 捍衛人權 (uphold human rights). More vigorous and combative than 維護 (maintain/protect — implies ongoing care) or 保護 (protect — general). 捍衛 implies there's something to fight against; you're defending against encroachment. Formal register; common in political speech and editorial writing.

examples.chinese: 我們有責任捍衛言論自由。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yǒu zérèn hànwèi yánlùn zìyóu.
examples.english: We have a responsibility to defend freedom of speech.

examples.chinese: 士兵們用生命捍衛了這片土地。
examples.pinyin: Shìbīngmen yòng shēngmìng hànwèile zhè piàn tǔdì.
examples.english: The soldiers defended this land with their lives.

semanticNote: A line or column of people or things — a procession, a rank. 加入行列 (join the ranks) is very common figuratively: 加入志工行列 (join the volunteer ranks), 加入創業行列 (join the entrepreneurial ranks). The literal meaning (rows and columns) is less common than the figurative 'ranks of a group or movement.' Don't confuse with 行業 (industry/trade).

examples.chinese: 越來越多年輕人加入創業的行列。
examples.pinyin: Yuè lái yuè duō niánqīngrén jiārù chuàngyè de hángliè.
examples.english: More and more young people are joining the ranks of entrepreneurs.

examples.chinese: 遊行的行列綿延了好幾個街區。
examples.pinyin: Yóuxíng de hángliè miányánle hǎo jǐ ge jiēqū.
examples.english: The parade procession stretched for several city blocks.

semanticNote: Aviation as an industry or domain — 航空公司 (airline), 民用航空 (civil aviation), 航空母艦 (aircraft carrier — lit. aviation mother ship). Common in airline names: 中華航空 (China Airlines), 長榮航空 (EVA Air). Different from 航天 (space flight — beyond the atmosphere). 航空 = flight within the atmosphere; 航天 = space travel.

components.meaning: to navigate; to fly; to sail

examples.chinese: 她在一家國際航空公司擔任空服員。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yī jiā guójì hángkōng gōngsī dānrèn kōngfúyuán.
examples.english: She works as a flight attendant for an international airline.

examples.chinese: 航空業受到疫情的嚴重衝擊。
examples.pinyin: Hángkōngyè shòudào yìqíng de yánzhòng chōngjī.
examples.english: The aviation industry was severely impacted by the pandemic.

semanticNote: The Chinese term for space travel and astronautics — 航天員 (astronaut/taikonaut), 航天飛機 (space shuttle), 航天工程 (space engineering). Mainland Chinese prefer 航天員 over 太空人 (the Taiwan term for astronaut). The distinction: 航空 = atmospheric flight, 航天 = space (lit. 'navigating the heavens'). Taiwan uses 太空 more commonly for space; 航天 is more of a mainland PRC technical term.

examples.chinese: 中國的航天技術近年來取得了重大突破。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó de hángtiān jìshù jìnnián lái qǔdéle zhòngdà túpò.
examples.english: China's space technology has made major breakthroughs in recent years.

examples.chinese: 他從小就夢想成為一名航天員。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng xiǎo jiù mèngxiǎng chéngwéi yī míng hángtiānyuán.
examples.english: He's dreamed of becoming an astronaut since he was a child.

english: to sail; to navigate; to fly
semanticNote: The act of navigating — by sea, air, or space. 輪船在海上航行 (the ship sails at sea), 飛機正在航行中 (the plane is in flight). More formal and technical than 開船 (to operate a ship) or 飛行 (to fly). Emphasizes the journey and navigation aspect rather than the mechanics. Common in formal reports, weather updates, and maritime/aviation news.

components.meaning: to travel; to go; to move

examples.chinese: 這艘船將航行三個月才能抵達目的地。
examples.pinyin: Zhè sōu chuán jiāng hángxíng sān ge yuè cái néng dǐdá mùdìdì.
examples.english: This ship will sail for three months before reaching its destination.

examples.chinese: 飛機正在太平洋上空航行。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī zhèngzài Tàipíngyáng shàngkōng hángxíng.
examples.english: The plane is currently flying over the Pacific Ocean.

semanticNote: The unit millimeter — used in engineering, medicine, weather (rainfall), and photography (lens focal length). 毫 = one-thousandth (also used in 毫升 milliliter, 毫克 milligram). Very precise measurement contexts. In Taiwan everyday speech you might say 一毫米都不差 (not off by a millimeter) to mean something is exact. A 50毫米鏡頭 = a 50mm lens.

examples.chinese: 今天的降雨量只有零點五毫米。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de jiàngyǔliàng zhǐyǒu líng diǎn wǔ háomǐ.
examples.english: Today's rainfall was only 0.5 millimeters.

examples.chinese: 這個零件的誤差不能超過兩毫米。
examples.pinyin: Zhège língjiàn de wùchā bù néng chāoguò liǎng háomǐ.
examples.english: The tolerance on this part cannot exceed two millimeters.

english: not at all; completely without; without the slightest
semanticNote: Emphatic 'not at all' — completely devoid of something. 毫無根據 (without any basis), 毫無疑問 (without a doubt), 毫無道理 (utterly unreasonable). Always followed by a noun. The 毫 (a hair's breadth) makes it emphatic — not even the tiniest amount. 毫無疑問 is one of the most common phrases using it — equivalent to 'without a doubt' or 'undoubtedly.'

components.meaning: hair; tiny; not in the least

examples.chinese: 這個指控毫無根據，完全是捏造的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zhǐkòng háowú gēnjù, wánquán shì niēzào de.
examples.english: This accusation is completely baseless — pure fabrication.

examples.chinese: 毫無疑問，她是這次比賽最出色的選手。
examples.pinyin: Háowú yíwèn, tā shì zhè cì bǐsài zuì chūsè de xuǎnshǒu.
examples.english: Without a doubt, she was the standout player in this competition.

semanticNote: A bold, sweeping, uninhibited spirit — the quality of someone who lives and acts on a grand scale. 性格豪邁 (bold/magnanimous personality), 豪邁的氣概 (heroic bearing), 舉止豪邁 (grand, unrestrained manner). Often applied to historical figures, warriors, poets, and strong personalities. The word has a romantically positive connotation — think of the Li Bai type, drinking wine and writing sweeping verse. Not reckless — more like grandly unencumbered.

examples.chinese: 他性格豪邁，朋友遍天下。
examples.pinyin: Tā xìnggé háomài, péngyou biàn tiānxià.
examples.english: He has a bold, magnanimous character — friends everywhere under heaven.

examples.chinese: 這首詩充滿了豪邁的氣概。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu shī chōngmǎnle háomài de qìgài.
examples.english: This poem is full of bold, heroic spirit.

english: call upon; appeal; summon (people to action)
semanticNote: A public call to action — a leader, movement, or cause calling people to rally. 號召人民 (call upon the people), 發出號召 (issue a call to action), 響應號召 (respond to the call). More mobilizing and rhetorical than 呼籲 (appeal — which can be quieter and more pleading). 號召 implies authority and expects a response; 呼籲 is more of a plea. Common in political, social, and wartime rhetoric.

examples.chinese: 他號召大家一起為環境保護出一份力。
examples.pinyin: Tā hàozhào dàjiā yīqǐ wèi huánjìng bǎohù chū yī fèn lì.
examples.english: He called on everyone to contribute to environmental protection.

examples.chinese: 政府發出號召，鼓勵民眾節約用水。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ fāchū hàozhào, gǔlì mínzhòng jiéyuē yòng shuǐ.
examples.english: The government issued a call for people to conserve water.

english: consume; expend; use up (resources, time, energy)
semanticNote: To consume or expend resources — often with a sense of waste or heavy cost. 耗費大量時間 (consume a lot of time), 耗費心血 (expend great effort/heart and blood), 耗費金錢 (spend money heavily). The 耗 implies draining or depleting, so it carries a negative undertone — this consumption is costly. Different from 花費 (spend — neutral) or 消費 (consume/spend — neutral/positive in consumer context).

examples.chinese: 這個計畫耗費了大量的人力和財力。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà hàofèile dàliàng de rénlì hé cáilì.
examples.english: This project consumed enormous human and financial resources.

examples.chinese: 長時間的談判耗費了雙方很多精力。
examples.pinyin: Cháng shíjiān de tánpàn hàofèile shuāngfāng hěn duō jīnglì.
examples.english: The prolonged negotiations drained a great deal of energy from both sides.

semanticNote: Multiple uses: (1) breathe out warm air — 呵手取暖 (breathe on hands to warm them); (2) scold — 呵斥 (reprimand sharply); (3) exclamatory particle 呵 hā/a — like 好呵 (how nice!), often written 啊 in modern text but appears as 呵 in older or literary usage. The scolding sense is most HSK-relevant: 呵斥 is a compound worth knowing.

examples.chinese: 天氣太冷，他不停地呵手取暖。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì tài lěng, tā bù tíng de hē shǒu qǔ nuǎn.
examples.english: It was so cold he kept breathing on his hands to warm them.

examples.chinese: 老師突然呵斥學生，全班都嚇了一跳。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī tūrán hēchì xuéshēng, quánbān dōu xiàle yī tiào.
examples.english: The teacher suddenly scolded the student sharply and the whole class jumped.

semanticNote: To merge or combine two or more things into one — companies, departments, organizations, illnesses. 公司合併 (company merger), 合併症 (complication — a disease combining with another condition), 兩班合併 (two classes merged into one). In medical contexts, 合併症 means a complication or comorbidity. Note: traditional form is 合併 (bìng with 幷); simplified 合并 uses a different 并.

examples.chinese: 兩家公司宣布合併，成立一家新企業。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng jiā gōngsī xuānbù hébìng, chénglì yī jiā xīn qǐyè.
examples.english: The two companies announced a merger and established a new enterprise.

examples.chinese: 學校因招生不足決定將兩個班合併。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào yīn zhāoshēng bùzú juédìng jiāng liǎng ge bān hébìng.
examples.english: Due to insufficient enrollment, the school decided to merge the two classes.

semanticNote: To synthesize or compose from parts — chemical synthesis (合成纖維 = synthetic fiber, 合成材料 = composite material), musical composition, or digital compositing (合成圖片 = composite image). 人工合成 = artificially synthesized. Common across chemistry, music production, and digital media. 合成音樂 = synthesized music. In modern usage often appears in creative/tech contexts.

components.meaning: to form; to become; to accomplish

examples.chinese: 這件衣服是合成纖維製成的，不容易皺。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu shì héchéng xiānwéi zhìchéng de, bù róngyì zhòu.
examples.english: This garment is made of synthetic fiber and doesn't wrinkle easily.

examples.chinese: 科學家已能人工合成這種化合物。
examples.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā yǐ néng réngōng héchéng zhè zhǒng huàhéwù.
examples.english: Scientists can now artificially synthesize this compound.

english: form a partnership; go into business together
semanticNote: To join forces with someone, especially in a business venture — 合夥開公司 (start a company together), 合夥人 (business partner). Can also be used colloquially about jointly doing something: 合夥騙人 (conspire to deceive someone). The business-partnership sense is dominant. Different from 合作 (cooperate/collaborate — broader, can be temporary or one-project); 合夥 implies shared ownership or ongoing joint enterprise.

examples.chinese: 他們三個人合夥開了一家咖啡廳。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen sān ge rén héhuǒ kāile yī jiā kāfēitīng.
examples.english: The three of them went into business together and opened a café.

examples.chinese: 找合夥人之前，最好簽訂書面協議。
examples.pinyin: Zhǎo héhuǒ rén zhīqián, zuì hǎo qiāndìng shūmiàn xiéyì.
examples.english: Before bringing on a business partner, it's best to sign a written agreement.

semanticNote: Something that's worth it — good value for money or effort. 這樣做不合算 (it's not worth it to do it that way), 買這個很合算 (buying this is a good deal). Primarily about economic/practical value calculation. Colloquial and everyday — much more common in casual speech than formal writing. Compare to 划算 (同義詞 — essentially synonymous and very commonly used in Taiwan: 很划算 = great value).

examples.chinese: 買這個套餐比單點要合算得多。
examples.pinyin: Mǎi zhège tàocān bǐ dān diǎn yào hésuàn de duō.
examples.english: Getting the set meal is much more worthwhile than ordering individually.

examples.chinese: 開車去還是搭捷運比較合算？
examples.pinyin: Kāichē qù háishi dā jiéyùn bǐjiào hésuàn?
examples.english: Is it more cost-effective to drive or take the MRT?

semanticNote: A warm, gentle, approachable manner — 和藹可親 (kind and approachable, a set phrase) is the most common extended form. Often used to describe elders, teachers, or respected figures who are warm and easy to talk to. 和藹的老師 (a kind teacher), 態度和藹 (an amiable manner). More literary/formal than 親切 (warm and friendly — the everyday word). 和藹 has a gentle, almost elderly warmth to it.

examples.chinese: 他是一個和藹可親的老師，學生都很喜歡他。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge hé'ǎi kěqīn de lǎoshī, xuéshēng dōu hěn xǐhuān tā.
examples.english: He's a kind and approachable teacher — all the students adore him.

examples.chinese: 老奶奶和藹地招手讓孩子過來。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo nǎinai hé'ǎi de zhāoshǒu ràng háizi guòlái.
examples.english: The elderly woman kindly waved for the child to come over.

english: reconciliation; settle (a dispute); reach a settlement
semanticNote: To resolve a conflict and reach peace — in personal relationships, legal cases, or international disputes. 庭外和解 (out-of-court settlement), 雙方達成和解 (both sides reached a settlement), 與過去和解 (reconcile with the past). Legal and diplomatic use is frequent. Also used in emotional/personal contexts: 她終於和自己的父親和解了 (she finally reconciled with her father). Implies mutual agreement, not unilateral forgiveness.

examples.chinese: 兩個家庭在法庭外達成了和解。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng ge jiātíng zài fǎtíng wài dádéle héjiě.
examples.english: The two families reached an out-of-court settlement.

examples.chinese: 多年的誤會之後，他們終於和解了。
examples.pinyin: Duō nián de wùhuì zhīhòu, tāmen zhōngyú héjiě le.
examples.english: After years of misunderstanding, they finally reconciled.

semanticNote: Living or getting along in harmony — 家庭和睦 (a harmonious family), 和睦相處 (get along harmoniously). Describes the ongoing state of peaceful relations between people who live or work together. More interpersonal and domestic than 和諧 (harmonious — which is broader and includes social/systemic harmony). 和睦 is specifically about relationship quality between people: neighbors, family members, colleagues.

examples.chinese: 他們一家人關係和睦，從不爭吵。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen yī jiā rén guānxì hémù, cóng bù zhēngchǎo.
examples.english: Their family gets along harmoniously — they never quarrel.

examples.chinese: 鄰居之間和睦相處是社區幸福的基礎。
examples.pinyin: Línjū zhījiān hémù xiāngchǔ shì shèqū xìngfú de jīchǔ.
examples.english: Neighbors getting along harmoniously is the foundation of a happy community.

semanticNote: A pleasant, easy-going manner in dealing with others — 態度和氣 (a friendly manner), 待人和氣 (treat people kindly). More about behavioral manner than inner character: a 和氣 person is pleasant to deal with. Common chengyu: 和氣生財 (a friendly manner generates wealth — good for business). In Taiwan business culture this is a highly valued quality in service staff and salespeople.

examples.chinese: 這位老闆待人和氣，員工都很尊敬他。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎobǎn dàirén héqi, yuángōng dōu hěn zūnjìng tā.
examples.english: This boss treats people with a friendly manner and all the employees respect him.

examples.chinese: 做生意要和氣生財，不能太強硬。
examples.pinyin: Zuò shēngyi yào héqi shēngcái, bù néng tài qiángyìng.
examples.english: In business, a friendly manner brings prosperity — you can't be too aggressive.

semanticNote: Harmony at a broader level — social, aesthetic, systemic. 和諧社會 (harmonious society — a PRC political slogan), 色彩和諧 (colors in harmony), 音樂和諧 (musical harmony). More abstract and formal than 和睦 (which is about interpersonal relations). Taiwan note: 被和諧 (to be 'harmonized') is PRC internet slang for censored content — ironic usage well-known in Chinese-speaking internet culture.

examples.chinese: 這幅畫的色彩搭配非常和諧。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fú huà de sècǎi dāpèi fēicháng héxié.
examples.english: The color combination in this painting is extremely harmonious.

examples.chinese: 社會和諧需要每個人的共同努力。
examples.pinyin: Shèhuì héxié xūyào měi ge rén de gòngtóng nǔlì.
examples.english: Social harmony requires the collective effort of everyone.

english: hey; interjection to get attention or express surprise
semanticNote: A natural, versatile interjection. (1) Getting someone's attention: 嘿！你在幹嘛？(Hey! What are you doing?); (2) Expressing surprise or discovery: 嘿，這個辦法還真管用！(Hey, this method actually works!); (3) Smugly noting something: 嘿嘿 (a knowing chuckle, slightly smug or sly). More colloquial and punchy than 喂 (used mainly on the phone or to interrupt). Tone is often playful.

examples.chinese: 嘿，你昨天怎麼沒來？
examples.pinyin: Hēi, nǐ zuótiān zěnme méi lái?
examples.english: Hey, how come you didn't show up yesterday?

examples.chinese: 嘿！這個主意真不錯！
examples.pinyin: Hēi! Zhège zhǔyì zhēn búcuò!
examples.english: Hey! That's a really good idea!

semanticNote: A mark or trace left behind — physically (血跡、抓痕 — blood stains, scratch marks) or metaphorically (歲月的痕跡 = traces of time, 歷史的痕跡 = vestiges of history). 留下痕跡 (leave a trace), 沒有任何痕跡 (without a trace). In forensic/mystery contexts: 現場沒有留下任何痕跡 (the scene left no trace). Also used for emotional marks: 在心上留下痕跡 (leave a mark on one's heart).

examples.chinese: 牆上有被刮過的痕跡。
examples.pinyin: Qiáng shàng yǒu bèi guāguò de hénjì.
examples.english: There are scratch marks on the wall.

examples.chinese: 這段感情在她心上留下了深刻的痕跡。
examples.pinyin: Zhè duàn gǎnqíng zài tā xīn shàng liúxiàle shēnkè de hénjì.
examples.english: This relationship left a deep mark on her heart.

english: hard-hearted; callous; steeling oneself (to do something hard)
semanticNote: Two registers: (1) descriptive — someone cold-hearted or cruel: 他狠心地拋棄了她 (he heartlessly abandoned her); (2) the act of steeling oneself to do something emotionally difficult but necessary: 她狠下心來結束了這段感情 (she steeled herself and ended the relationship). The second sense is empathetic — you feel for the person who has to be 狠心 because it's hard. Context distinguishes the two.

examples.chinese: 她狠下心來，辭掉了那份做了十年的工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn xià xīn lái, cídiào le nà fèn zuòle shí nián de gōngzuò.
examples.english: She steeled herself and quit the job she'd held for ten years.

examples.chinese: 他真夠狠心的，一句話都沒說就離開了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhēn gòu hěnxīn de, yī jù huà dōu méi shuō jiù líkāile.
examples.english: He was really heartless — left without saying a single word.

english: wish one could; be dying to; itch to
semanticNote: Expresses an intense wish to do something — usually something impossible, exaggerated, or strongly desired. 我恨不得馬上飛回家 (I wish I could fly home right now), 她恨不得把那本書一口氣看完 (she was dying to read that book in one sitting). Always followed by a verb phrase. The 'regret/wish' framing (恨 = hate/regret) shows the intensity — you hate that you CAN'T. Very colloquial and vivid.

examples.chinese: 他恨不得把時間倒回去，重新選擇。
examples.pinyin: Tā hènbude bǎ shíjiān dào huíqù, chóngxīn xuǎnzé.
examples.english: He wishes he could turn back time and choose differently.

examples.chinese: 天氣太熱了，我恨不得跳進游泳池裡。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì tài rè le, wǒ hènbude tiào jìn yóuyǒngchí lǐ.
examples.english: It's so hot — I'm dying to just jump in the swimming pool.

semanticNote: Primary meaning: horizontal or across — 橫線 (horizontal line), 橫掃 (sweep across). Also means willful or perverse — 蠻橫 (overbearing and unreasonable). In writing, 橫 (horizontal stroke) is one of the eight basic brush strokes. Key compound: 橫豎 (anyway/in any case — colloquial: 橫豎都是我的錯 = it's my fault either way). Also 橫衝直撞 (rushing around recklessly).

examples.chinese: 請在這裡畫一條橫線。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ huà yī tiáo héngxiàn.
examples.english: Please draw a horizontal line here.

examples.chinese: 他態度蠻橫，根本不聽別人說話。
examples.pinyin: Tā tàidù mánhéng, gēnběn bù tīng biérén shuōhuà.
examples.english: He's overbearing and unreasonable — doesn't listen to anyone at all.

semanticNote: Three distinct uses: (1) hum a tune — 哼著歌走路 (walk along humming a song); (2) groan in pain — 他痛得哼了一聲 (he groaned in pain); (3) snort of contempt — 哼！你以為我不知道嗎！ (Hmph! You think I don't know?). The contemptuous snort is the most dramatic and narratively useful. In fiction, 她哼了一聲 signals displeasure or disdain.

examples.chinese: 他受傷後痛得哼了幾聲。
examples.pinyin: Tā shòushāng hòu tòng de hēngle jǐ shēng.
examples.english: After getting hurt, he groaned a few times in pain.

examples.chinese: 哼！你說的話我才不信呢。
examples.pinyin: Hēng! Nǐ shuō de huà wǒ cái bú xìn ne.
examples.english: Hmph! I don't believe a word you're saying.

english: cause a sensation; make a big stir
semanticNote: To cause a sensation — big news, a shocking event, a viral moment. 轟動全國 (a nationwide sensation), 轟動一時 (a sensation at the time), 引起轟動 (caused a stir). 轟 is the sound of rumbling or explosion — 轟動 is something that metaphorically shakes people. Always significant and public; you can't have a private 轟動. Common in entertainment, news, and social media contexts.

examples.chinese: 這部電影一上映就引起了巨大轟動。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng yī shàngyìng jiù yǐnqǐle jùdà hōngdòng.
examples.english: As soon as this film was released, it caused a massive sensation.

examples.chinese: 這則新聞轟動了整個社群媒體。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zé xīnwén hōngdòngle zhěng ge shèqún méitǐ.
examples.english: This piece of news sent shockwaves across all social media.

english: bake; dry by heat; set off by contrast
semanticNote: To dry or warm something with heat — 烘乾 (dry with heat/blow-dry), 烘焙 (bake — as in baking bread/pastries), 烘手機 (hand dryer). 烘焙 is very common in Taiwan's café culture. The literary sense 烘托 (set off by contrast, render more vivid through contrast) is important in writing analysis: 用景色烘托情感 (use scenery to heighten the emotional atmosphere).

components.meaning: warm by fire; bake; set off

examples.chinese: 她把濕衣服放進烘乾機裡烘乾。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ shī yīfu fàngjìn hōnggānjī lǐ hōng gān.
examples.english: She put the wet clothes in the dryer to dry them.

examples.chinese: 這家麵包店的烘焙香氣飄滿了整條街。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā miànbāodiàn de hōngbèi xiānqì piāo mǎnle zhěng tiáo jiē.
examples.english: The baking aroma from this bakery filled the entire street.

semanticNote: The macro-level view — broad, systemic, top-down. 宏觀經濟 (macroeconomics), 宏觀調控 (macro-level regulation), 從宏觀角度看 (viewed from a macro perspective). Paired antonym: 微觀 (micro-; microscopic). Common in economics, policy, and academic discussion. In Taiwan business analysis: 宏觀環境分析 (macro-environmental analysis = PEST analysis).

examples.chinese: 我們需要從宏觀的角度來分析這個問題。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào cóng hóngguān de jiǎodù lái fēnxī zhège wèntí.
examples.english: We need to analyze this problem from a macro perspective.

examples.chinese: 宏觀經濟的穩定對企業發展至關重要。
examples.pinyin: Hóngguān jīngjì de wěndìng duì qǐyè fāzhǎn zhìguān zhòngyào.
examples.english: Macroeconomic stability is crucial for business development.

semanticNote: Grand in scale and impressive — 宏偉的建築 (a magnificent building), 宏偉的目標 (an ambitious/grand goal), 氣勢宏偉 (impressively grand in presence). Emphasizes scale and grandeur. Similar to 壯觀 (spectacular — more about the visual spectacle) and 雄偉 (imposing/majestic — often used for mountains and natural features). 宏偉 can apply to both physical structures and abstract ambitions.

examples.chinese: 故宮的建築宏偉壯觀，令人嘆為觀止。
examples.pinyin: Gùgōng de jiànzhú hóngwěi zhuàngguān, lìng rén tàn wéi guān zhǐ.
examples.english: The Forbidden City's architecture is grand and spectacular — truly breathtaking.

examples.chinese: 他們提出了一個宏偉的城市發展計畫。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen tíchūle yí ge hóngwěi de chéngshì fāzhǎn jìhuà.
examples.english: They put forward a grand plan for urban development.

semanticNote: Floodwaters — a natural disaster. 洪水泛濫 (flooding everywhere), 抗洪救災 (flood control and disaster relief). Common in news coverage of Taiwan typhoon seasons. Figurative use: 洪水猛獸 (a phrase meaning something extremely dangerous — lit. 'flood and fierce beast'). Taiwan is hit regularly by typhoon-related flooding, so 洪水 is a culturally resonant word.

examples.chinese: 颱風過後，山區爆發了嚴重的洪水。
examples.pinyin: Táifēng guòhòu, shānqū bàofāle yánzhòng de hóngshuǐ.
examples.english: After the typhoon, severe flooding broke out in the mountain areas.

examples.chinese: 政府緊急疏散了洪水災區的居民。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ jǐnjí shūsànle hóngshuǐ zāiqū de jūmín.
examples.english: The government urgently evacuated residents from the flood-affected areas.

semanticNote: To soothe or coax someone — especially a child or an upset person — through gentle words, tricks, or play. 哄孩子 (coax a child), 哄她開心 (try to cheer her up), 被人哄了 (got fooled/tricked). The coaxing sense is warm; the fooling sense is slightly negative. Note: 哄 hōng (first tone) means a crowd making noise — 哄堂大笑 (the whole room burst out laughing). The coax/fool sense is third tone hǒng.

examples.chinese: 寶寶一直哭，媽媽用玩具哄他。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao yīzhí kū, māma yòng wánjù hǒng tā.
examples.english: The baby kept crying, so mom used a toy to soothe him.

examples.chinese: 別被他的甜言蜜語哄了，他說話不算數。
examples.pinyin: Bié bèi tā de tiányánmìyǔ hǒng le, tā shuōhuà bú suàn shù.
examples.english: Don't be fooled by his sweet talk — he never keeps his word.

semanticNote: The throat — everyday body part word. 喉嚨痛 (sore throat — one of the most common phrases), 清清喉嚨 (clear one's throat), 喉嚨啞了 (lost one's voice). 喉嚨 refers to the general throat area; more technical terms: 喉頭 (larynx), 咽喉 (pharynx and larynx). In Taiwan: 喉嚨不舒服 (my throat is bothering me) is extremely common when getting sick.

examples.chinese: 我喉嚨痛了好幾天，可能感冒了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hóulóng tòngle hǎo jǐ tiān, kěnéng gǎnmào le.
examples.english: My throat has been sore for several days — I might have a cold.

examples.chinese: 她演講前先清了清喉嚨。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǎnjiǎng qián xiān qīngle qīng hóulóng.
examples.english: She cleared her throat before the speech.

semanticNote: A loud, rough cry — an animal's roar or a person bellowing. 獅子吼 (lion's roar), 他對著我大吼 (he bellowed at me). In Taiwanese colloquial speech, 吼 is also a softened exclamation particle similar to 喔/啊 — written 吼 when mimicking a nasal Taiwanese-accented Mandarin sound. In standard Mandarin, it's strictly roar/shout.

examples.chinese: 老虎突然發出一聲低沉的吼聲。
examples.pinyin: Lǎohǔ tūrán fāchū yī shēng dīchén de hǒu shēng.
examples.english: The tiger suddenly let out a deep, low roar.

examples.chinese: 他氣到對著電話大吼起來。
examples.pinyin: Tā qì dào duìzhe diànhuà dà hǒu qǐlái.
examples.english: He got so angry he started bellowing into the phone.

semanticNote: Descendants or future generations — 為後代著想 (think of future generations), 留給後代 (leave to posterity), 子孫後代 (descendants and heirs). More formal and broad than 子女 (children) or 後裔 (descendants — same meaning but 後裔 is more specifically lineage-based). Common in environmental, historical, and legacy contexts. 造福後代 (benefit future generations) is a common phrase in policy and environmental writing.

examples.chinese: 我們有責任為後代保護好這片土地。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yǒu zérèn wèi hòudài bǎohù hǎo zhè piàn tǔdì.
examples.english: We have a responsibility to preserve this land for future generations.

examples.chinese: 這些古老的技藝需要傳給後代。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē gǔlǎo de jìyì xūyào chuán gěi hòudài.
examples.english: These ancient crafts need to be passed down to future generations.

english: worries about problems from behind; concerns about the home front
semanticNote: Literally 'worries from looking behind' — concerns about problems at home or in the rear while you're occupied elsewhere. Almost always appears in the negative: 沒有後顧之憂 (without worries back home / free from concerns at the rear). 解決後顧之憂 = take care of concerns on the home front. If you're going to start a business, having savings 解決後顧之憂 means you can focus on the venture without worrying about money.

examples.chinese: 有了這筆存款，他創業時就沒有後顧之憂了。
examples.pinyin: Yǒule zhè bǐ cúnkuǎn, tā chuàngyè shí jiù méiyǒu hòugùzhīyōu le.
examples.english: With these savings, he had no worries on the home front when starting his business.

examples.chinese: 公司提供員工宿舍，讓外地員工沒有後顧之憂。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī tígōng yuángōng sùshè, ràng wàidì yuángōng méiyǒu hòugùzhīyōu.
examples.english: The company provides staff housing so out-of-town employees have no home front worries.

semanticNote: Logistics — originally a military term for supply and support operations at the rear. Now used broadly in business and event planning: 後勤人員 (logistics staff), 後勤工作 (logistical work), 活動後勤 (event logistics). The unsung support work that keeps operations running. In Taiwan, 後勤 is increasingly common in corporate and startup language as supply chains and operations become more prominent.

examples.chinese: 這次活動的後勤工作非常複雜，需要大量人手。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì huódòng de hòuqín gōngzuò fēicháng fùzá, xūyào dàliàng rénshǒu.
examples.english: The logistics for this event are very complex and require a lot of manpower.

examples.chinese: 她負責整個公司的後勤管理。
examples.pinyin: Tā fùzé zhěng ge gōngsī de hòuqín guǎnlǐ.
examples.english: She's responsible for the entire company's logistics management.

semanticNote: Being a candidate — 候選人 (candidate), 候選名單 (list of candidates), 候選資格 (candidacy qualification). Used in political elections, award nominations, and job selection processes. In Taiwan's active democratic culture, 候選人 appears constantly during election season. Different from 應試者 (exam candidate) or 求職者 (job applicant) — 候選 specifically implies being put forward for selection.

examples.chinese: 她是這次市長選舉的候選人之一。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì zhè cì shìzhǎng xuǎnjǔ de hòuxuǎnrén zhī yī.
examples.english: She is one of the candidates in this mayoral election.

examples.chinese: 這部電影被提名為最佳影片候選。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng bèi tímíng wéi zuìjiā yǐngpiàn hòuxuǎn.
examples.english: This film was nominated as a Best Picture candidate.

semanticNote: To call someone's name or call out to them — can be literal (呼喚孩子回家 = call the child home) or figurative (時代的呼喚 = the call of the times; 良知的呼喚 = the call of conscience). The figurative use is very literary and common in essays and speeches. 呼喚 is warmer and more personal than 呼叫 (call/alert — more mechanical, like calling an emergency service).

examples.chinese: 她站在門口大聲呼喚孩子的名字。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhàn zài ménkǒu dàshēng hūhuàn háizi de míngzì.
examples.english: She stood at the doorway calling out the child's name.

examples.chinese: 這個時代呼喚更多有責任感的年輕人。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shídài hūhuàn gèng duō yǒu zérèngǎn de niánqīngrén.
examples.english: This era calls for more young people with a sense of responsibility.

semanticNote: A high-pitched rushing sound — wind howling, a train or bullet whooshing past. 寒風呼嘯 (cold wind howling), 子彈呼嘯而過 (bullets whistling past), 列車呼嘯而過 (the train whooshed by). Very evocative and literary — commonly used in fiction to set atmosphere. Not used for human voices (that would be 嚎叫 or 尖叫); 呼嘯 is for non-human sounds of speed or wind.

examples.chinese: 颱風來臨，狂風呼嘯整夜未停。
examples.pinyin: Táifēng láilín, kuángfēng hūxiào zhěng yè wèi tíng.
examples.english: As the typhoon approached, the fierce wind howled all night without stopping.

examples.chinese: 高鐵呼嘯而過，轉眼便消失在視線中。
examples.pinyin: Gāotiě hūxiào ér guò, zhuǎnyǎn biàn xiāoshī zài shìxiàn zhōng.
examples.english: The high-speed train whooshed past and vanished from sight in an instant.

semanticNote: A public appeal or plea — calling on people or institutions to act. 呼籲政府重視此問題 (appeal to the government to address this issue), 發出呼籲 (issue an appeal), 國際社會的呼籲 (the international community's appeals). More pleading and earnest than 號召 (which is more authoritative and mobilizing). Common in civil society, human rights, and environmental contexts. In Taiwan: NGOs and activists 呼籲 frequently.

examples.chinese: 環保團體呼籲民眾減少一次性塑膠的使用。
examples.pinyin: Huánbǎo tuántǐ hūyù mínzhòng jiǎnshǎo yīcìxìng sùjiāo de shǐyòng.
examples.english: Environmental groups are appealing to the public to reduce single-use plastic.

examples.chinese: 他在記者會上呼籲雙方保持冷靜。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jìzhě huì shàng hūyù shuāngfāng bǎochí lěngjìng.
examples.english: He appealed to both sides at the press conference to stay calm.

semanticNote: To overlook or fail to notice — often unintentionally. 忽略細節 (overlook details), 不可忽略 (cannot be overlooked), 被忽略的問題 (overlooked issues). Different from 忽視 (ignore/disregard — often implies awareness and deliberate dismissal) and 漠視 (turn a blind eye — stronger indifference). 忽略 is the mildest: you just missed it. 忽視 = you knew but didn't care. 漠視 = you coldly turned away.

examples.chinese: 他太專注於工作，忽略了家人的感受。
examples.pinyin: Tā tài zhuānzhù yú gōngzuò, hūlüèle jiārén de gǎnshòu.
examples.english: He was so focused on work that he overlooked his family's feelings.

examples.chinese: 報告中有幾個重要細節被忽略了。
examples.pinyin: Bàogào zhōng yǒu jǐ ge zhòngyào xìjié bèi hūlüè le.
examples.english: Several important details in the report were overlooked.

semanticNote: Doing something carelessly, randomly, or without proper thought. 胡亂說話 (talk recklessly/say things carelessly), 胡亂猜測 (guess wildly), 胡亂吃東西 (eat haphazardly). Slightly negative — implies the action was irresponsible or thoughtless. Colloquial. 胡 alone has a historical sense of 'foreign/barbarian' that evolved into 'wild/nonsensical' — 胡說 (nonsense!), 胡鬧 (cause trouble/misbehave).

examples.chinese: 你別胡亂說話，這樣會傷到別人的。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié húluàn shuōhuà, zhèyàng huì shāng dào biérén de.
examples.english: Don't say things carelessly — you'll end up hurting people.

examples.chinese: 這份報告是胡亂寫的，根本沒有邏輯。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn bàogào shì húluàn xiě de, gēnběn méiyǒu luójí.
examples.english: This report was thrown together carelessly — there's no logic to it at all.

semanticNote: Facial hair — beard, moustache, whiskers. 留鬍鬚 (grow a beard), 刮鬍鬚 (shave), 鬍子 (colloquial version — same meaning, shorter). Traditional form 鬍鬚 uses the 鬍 with the hair radical; simplified conflates to 胡须. In Taiwan, 鬍子 is the most common spoken form; 鬍鬚 appears in more formal or literary writing. 絡腮鬍 = full beard, 八字鬍 = handlebar moustache.

examples.chinese: 他留著一把濃密的鬍鬚，看起來很成熟。
examples.pinyin: Tā liúzhe yī bǎ nóngmì de húxū, kànqǐlái hěn chéngshú.
examples.english: He has a thick beard that makes him look very mature.

examples.chinese: 面試前記得把鬍鬚刮乾淨。
examples.pinyin: Miànshì qián jìde bǎ húxū guā gānjìng.
examples.english: Remember to shave your facial hair clean before the interview.

semanticNote: Lakes in general — a collective or literary term. 江河湖泊 (rivers and lakes — a common grouping), 保護湖泊 (protect lakes). More formal and literary than simply 湖 (lake — the everyday word). You'd say 我去了一個湖 (I went to a lake) in speech, but 湖泊資源 (lake resources) in a policy document. Common in environmental and geographic writing.

examples.chinese: 台灣的湖泊資源豐富，日月潭是其中最著名的。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān de húpō zīyuán fēngfù, Rìyuètán shì qízhōng zuì zhùmíng de.
examples.english: Taiwan is rich in lakes, with Sun Moon Lake being the most famous.

examples.chinese: 工業廢水污染了許多湖泊和河流。
examples.pinyin: Gōngyè fèishuǐ wūrǎnle xǔduō húpō hé héliú.
examples.english: Industrial wastewater has polluted many lakes and rivers.

semanticNote: A flower petal — 玫瑰花瓣 (rose petals), 花瓣飄落 (petals falling). Purely descriptive botanical/poetic term. Common in literary and romantic contexts: 花瓣 scattered on the ground or floating on water is a classic imagery cue. Also the name of a popular Chinese image-sharing platform (花瓣網 — like Pinterest). Not particularly tricky; just know the character 瓣 (which also appears in 瓣膜 = valve).

examples.chinese: 春風吹過，粉色的花瓣紛紛飄落。
examples.pinyin: Chūnfēng chuī guò, fěnsè de huābàn fēnfēn piāo luò.
examples.english: The spring breeze blew through and pink petals drifted down.

examples.chinese: 她把玫瑰花瓣撒在浴缸裡，營造浪漫氣氛。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ méigui huābàn sā zài yùgāng lǐ, yíngzào làngmàn qìfēn.
examples.english: She scattered rose petals in the bathtub to create a romantic atmosphere.

semanticNote: A flower bud — before it blooms. 含苞待放的花蕾 (a bud about to bloom) is a beautiful literary phrase often used to describe youth and potential. 蕾 specifically means bud; the character also appears in 蕾絲 (lace — transliteration). Literary and poetic word; not frequently used in everyday speech but appears in writing, nature descriptions, and metaphors about young people's potential.

examples.chinese: 枝頭上的花蕾即將在春天綻放。
examples.pinyin: Zhī tóu shàng de huālěi jíjiāng zài chūntiān zhànfàng.
examples.english: The buds on the branches will soon bloom in spring.

examples.chinese: 她就像一朵含苞待放的花蕾，充滿了無限可能。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiù xiàng yī duǒ hánbāo dài fàng de huālěi, chōngmǎnle wúxiàn kěnéng.
examples.english: She's like a flower bud about to bloom — full of infinite potential.

semanticNote: Gorgeous and ornate — 華麗的服裝 (gorgeous costume), 華麗的宮殿 (magnificent palace), 華麗的轉身 (a spectacular turnaround — lit. 'a gorgeous turn'). Can be used positively (truly beautiful) or slightly ironically (overly ornate, flashy). 華麗轉身 is a very common modern metaphor for a dramatic, successful transformation — a company's pivot, an athlete's comeback.

examples.chinese: 舞台上的表演者穿著華麗的戲服，令人眼花繚亂。
examples.pinyin: Wǔtái shàng de biǎoyǎnzhě chuānzhe huálì de xìfú, lìng rén yǎnhuā liáoluàn.
examples.english: The performers on stage wore gorgeous costumes that dazzled the eyes.

examples.chinese: 她在失業後完成了人生的華麗轉身，成為一名作家。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài shīyè hòu wánchéngle rénshēng de huálì zhuǎnshēn, chéngwéi yī míng zuòjiā.
examples.english: After losing her job, she made a spectacular turnaround and became a writer.

semanticNote: Chinese nationals living outside China — specifically those who retain their Chinese citizenship. 僑 means living abroad. Distinguished from 華裔 (ethnic Chinese who are citizens of another country) and 海外華人 (overseas Chinese — broad term). In Taiwan: 僑務委員會 (Overseas Community Affairs Council) handles 華僑 affairs. Important distinction: 華僑 = Chinese citizen abroad; 華裔美國人 = American of Chinese descent.

examples.chinese: 許多華僑雖然長年旅居海外，仍保有對故鄉的深厚感情。
examples.pinyin: Xǔduō huáqiáo suīrán chángnián lǚjū hǎiwài, réng bǎoyǒu duì gùxiāng de shēnhòu gǎnqíng.
examples.english: Many overseas Chinese, despite living abroad for years, still retain a deep affection for their homeland.

examples.chinese: 台灣每年吸引不少海外華僑回國投資。
examples.pinyin: Táiwān měi nián xīyǐn bùshǎo hǎiwài huáqiáo huíguó tóuzī.
examples.english: Every year Taiwan attracts many overseas Chinese to return and invest.

semanticNote: Chemical fertilizer — synthetic nutrients for agriculture. 施化肥 (apply fertilizer), 有機肥vs化肥 (organic fertilizer vs chemical fertilizer). In the context of food safety and organic farming discussions common in Taiwan, 化肥 often has a slightly negative connotation relative to 有機肥 (organic fertilizer). 化 here is short for 化學 (chemistry/chemical).

examples.chinese: 這個農場不使用化肥，全部採用有機耕作。
examples.pinyin: Zhège nóngchǎng bù shǐyòng huàféi, quánbù cǎiyòng yǒujī gēngzuò.
examples.english: This farm uses no chemical fertilizer — entirely organic farming.

examples.chinese: 過度使用化肥會破壞土壤的生態平衡。
examples.pinyin: Guòdù shǐyòng huàféi huì pòhuài tǔrǎng de shēngtài pínghéng.
examples.english: Excessive use of chemical fertilizer can destroy the soil's ecological balance.

semanticNote: A fossil — the preserved remains of ancient organisms. 恐龍化石 (dinosaur fossil), 化石燃料 (fossil fuels).
